# Playtest Backlog — Evidence Archive

Append-only cold storage for backlog evidence. The live index is
[`backlog.md`](./backlog.md); this file holds the investigation prose that used
to be interleaved with the table: follow-ups, notes, rejected hypotheses,
investigation write-ups, and dated playtest logs.

Keyed by issue id — grep `#NNN` (e.g. `grep -n '#238' backlog-archive.md`) to
recover an issue's full history. Order is the original `backlog.md` document
order at split time; nothing here is re-attributed or deduplicated.

---

### #418

Opened and closed 2026-07-20 (census ownership). The 106 blocking differences in
canonical sweep run `1783914264` (47/69 pass, 22 failing levels) had no
attribution: `StateDiff` names only global fields, so nothing tied a blocker to
an enemy family. Two-part fix: (1) `sweep-census` subcommand (mise
`sweep-census`; artefact `.cache/audit/sweep-census.json`) mechanically joins
blocking diffs (authoritative/accumulation/rng) onto per-level enemy-family
rosters via the new `wildside_core::layout_object_family_name` bridge, and ranks
families by Laplace-smoothed overrepresentation in failing vs passing levels;
(2) a 22-agent read-only attribution pass (one per failing level: blocking
diffs + roster + checkpoint/diff PNGs + family ASM + native family module)
returned per-level verdicts, synthesised into clusters #419-#433.

Cluster table (level: blockers, confidence):

|---|---|---|---|
| #419 | Goat | 0x38 (4), 0x60 (10), 0x63 (2) | high (0x60), medium |

Sums to 106. Census smoke checks: blocking total 106, failing levels 22,
per-level counts match the report (0x55=16, 0x41=12, 0x60=10), TarMonster near
the bottom of the suspect ratio table (0.62) as expected post-#402/#403.

Method notes: (a) levels without an enemy layout resource (0x41, 0x52) carry an
EMPTY roster — a real "not enemy-related" signal — distinct from a failed bundle
load, which excludes a level from the family table. (b) One agent claimed the
census mis-rostered 0x62 by reading raw `level/enemy/62.bin`; verified wrong —
logical 0x62 maps to resource 0x7D (`inspect-level --level 62`: Scorpion x3,
Drips x2, Armadillo x3), matching the census. Its behavioural evidence (oracle
Kid damaged on the spawn row, native untouched) still stands and re-attributes
to Scorpion (nearest enemy to spawn at 136,95), folded into #421 at medium.
(c) The family overrepresentation ratio is a suspect ranker, not proof; every
cluster row still requires probe-before-code per the loop protocol.

Common facts for #419-#433: evidence source `sweep:1783914264` + census +
attribution agents; native repro reproduced (idle scenario); oracle repro
status authoritative; minimum gate `fast-slice`.

### #419

Goat (0x38/0x60/0x63, 16 blockers). 0x60 (Goat-only roster, high): at
level_settle oracle Kid has just_received_damage=true, hitpoints 1, +1 object,
native false/2/-; idle_tail is pure cascade (native warps to the ELSEWHERE card
0x0008 vs InGame 0x000c and loses a life). Contact surface: Goat.asm contact
dispatch `loc_3CB14`/`loc_3CB38` recoil/`loc_3CB76` Berzerker, tracking
`loc_3CC52`; prior churn #057/#315/#331/#308. 0x38 (medium): pure count deficit
(-1 object, -2 gfx, MAE 0.0 — off-screen lifecycle). 0x63 (medium): +2 oracle
gfx = exactly the 2 roster Goats visible in oracle PNGs, native draws neither;
number_objects equal, so live slots match but two enemies never enter a drawn
state.

### #420

Driller (0x55/0x68, 19 blockers — largest cluster). 0x55 (Driller-only roster
x8): native Kid frozen at spawn, oracle Kid shows the golden Micromax transform
shimmer (helmet 9, currently_transforming, just_received_damage) with a Driller
beside him; count deltas (objects 4v7, gfx 5v12) match missing Drillers plus
tread/drill children (`loc_3BD74` spawns two children at parent ±$18). Caveat:
the Micromax transform is a prize interaction, so a prize/physics upstream
trigger is not fully excluded. 0x68 (Driller-only x7, high): counts only
(objects 6v8, gfx 7v15/13) — the Driller hidden-block/smash worker signature
(`sub_10EDA`, `loc_10F2A` hibernate); archive #385/#387 tie 0x68 to Driller
worker count parity (native `driller.rs` `loc_3BE78`/`loc_3BE60` refcount).

### #421

Scorpion (0x61/0x62, 10 blockers). 0x61 (high): native missing ~2 objects/~3
gfx; Scorpion.asm init allocates a linked tail/stinger gfx child
(`loc_3DC86`), so one missing scorpion drops 1 object + 2 gfx. diff PNG lights
up exactly on the two coil clusters; oracle Kid stung (`loc_3DCB0` dispatch,
sting `loc_3DDEE`) and knocked back, native Kid untouched. 0x62 (medium,
re-attributed from an agent misread — see #418 note b): oracle Kid damaged and
moving from the spawn row (HP 1→0), native Kid frozen/undamaged; Scorpions sit
on the spawn row at 136,95 (Kid start 32,80). #331's fixed candidate covered
the RockTank wall-turn, not these levels.

### #423

Ninja (0x56, 5 blockers). Roster is Ninja x4 exclusively, so family is certain;
mechanism is not. Native Kid takes a fatal hit on idle (lives 3→2, respawn HP
2) and sits mid-LevelTransition at idle_tail (0x0008, black frame) while oracle
Kid survives exactly one hit (HP 1, InGame). Native holds ~5 extra
Ninja-lineage objects (9v4 / gfx 8v5) — extra throws/undead Ninjas are the
plausible source of the extra fatal hit. Archive: hitpoints de-masking
(backlog-archive.md:13506) surfaced exactly this class; #315 holds prior Ninja
cadence/contact/i-frame work.

### #424

MiniHoppingSkull dormant controllers (0x44/0x65, 4 blockers).
`Enemy1C_MiniHoppingSkull_Init` (`loc_3E9C8`) hibernates in the `loc_3E9D0`
proximity loop and defers `Load_GfxObjectSlot` until Kid is near, so far-but-
in-window skulls exist as GfxObject-less live slots. 0x44: number_objects +5
oracle with gfx EQUAL — Object-only slots, exactly the dormant-skull signature
(roster MiniHoppingSkull x17; Dragon/DragonWalking excluded — their inits load
gfx immediately). 0x65 (MiniHoppingSkull-only roster): stable +1 object, no
other field diverges, divergent object off-screen. Native
`mini_hopping_skull.rs` models the active hop lifecycle but not the dormant
wait (archive #315 `loc_3EA88..loc_3F146` compression, #229 prior count
mismatches).

### #425

SpinningTwins leading spawn (0x47, 4 blockers). Oracle owns exactly one extra

### #426

Hand floor-scan deletion (0x59, 4 blockers). Roster 100% Hand (x5). Native +1
object/+1 gfx at both checkpoints = one whole surviving Hand (Hand init loads

### #429

Kid warp-settle wall nudge (0x29, 4 blockers) — root-caused. kid_x_pos native
0x02A0 vs oracle 0x02A5 (5px) with camera exactly 156px behind in both engines
(pure cascade). The respawn path already models the oracle-verified wall-nudge
to x=$02A50000 (#037/#049; guard
`respawn_settle_level_29_matches_oracle_wall_nudged_spawn_x` passes, gate
green), but the sweep's idle warp-settle path lands 5px left — the warp/initial
entry path misses the wall-overlap resolution the respawn slice applies.

Resolved 2026-07-20. The recording-oracle debug level-skip path deliberately
kept the raw header pose so Kid could settle under live gravity, but omitted
the source-ordered `loc_75C0 -> sub_7B30` spawn-overlap correction before
`loc_75D4`'s first camera tick and hibernate. `begin_debug_level_entry_loc_74e0`
now applies the shared engine-level overlap resolver without replacing the
live title-shell lifecycle with a synthetic floor snap.

The new cache-backed recording-warp regression failed at native
Kid/camera `$02A00000/$02040000` and passes at oracle
`$02A50000/$02090000` for frames 0 and 359. Existing respawn and bidirectional
wall-overlap guards remain green. Fresh Level 0x29 state report `1784577500`
passes both checkpoints with zero differences. Frame report `1784577515`
reduces the whole-scene shift from 40,822 changed pixels / MAE 34.0 to 1,072 /
MAE 1.6; the inspected residue is the existing right-edge background seam and
HUD diamond rendering debt, not Kid/camera state.

### #430

Kid vertical settle phase (0x52, 7 blockers, empty roster — zero enemies,
static `PlatformScript_Nothing` only). kid_y_vel at level_settle is native
-1.75px/f (up) vs oracle +1.75px/f (down): equal magnitude, opposite sign — a
spawn-drop landing one frame out of phase. kid_y never reconciles (native
pinned 342, oracle bobs 344→337); camera_y tracks 4px; the number_objects
5/3→3/5 swap is a slot-activation phase shift from the differing camera_y
revealing prize blocks, not a distinct object set.

### #431

Murder-wall settle (0x21, 2 blockers). murder_wall_x native ≈ -19.6px vs oracle
≈ +4.2px (~24px lag) and camera_x 0 vs 4px — the wall never pushed the camera.
Native surface: `step_murder_wall` (weather.rs) with
`forward_murder_wall_camera_push_loc_7346` and `init_murder_wall` seeding from
camera_x. Wall error is causal; camera_x is the downstream push. Archive
#266/#294/#335 cover the same subsystem on other levels; none owns 0x21.

### #432

0x42 high-skin decode (4 blockers) — the residual #330 already names
("unrelated level 0x42 city high-skin collision residual"). kid_y_pos native
351 vs oracle 367: exactly 16px = one tile, static from level_settle, no
object diffs; PNGs show Kid resting one tile high on the lamppost platform.
Suspect: city skin blank-top-row/high-skin collision-terrain decode
(`sub_140F6` / `Load_LevelData loc_15A0` family) offsetting the collision
surface one row.

### #433

Leftover level 0x41 classification (12 blockers). Roster empty; native
`load_level_visuals` deliberately skips 0x41 for missing foreground data
(#329: "0x41 still skips (no foreground)"), stalling in LevelTransition
(game_mode 0x0008, black frames), while the jgenesis oracle reads
adjacent/garbage RAM and reaches a settled InGame state. Every field diff is
downstream of comparing an unentered native level against oracle-played
garbage. Needs an evidence-backed sweep classification (`oracle_limitation`
with citation, or a decision to load the level) rather than 12 standing
authoritative blockers that verify nothing.

### #417

Opened 2026-07-20. `cargo test -p wildside-cli --no-fail-fast` has **55 committed
failures** on clean `main`, deterministic (identical membership across repeated
runs; libtest emits them alphabetically sorted). They rotted silently: the
canonical gate `verify-slice-fast` runs only `wildside-core --lib` +
`wildside-cli gameplay_regression_*`, and there is **no CI** (`.github/` does not
exist). The full `cargo test --workspace` (`mise run test`) is manual-only, so
nothing caught regressions in `native_player`, `inspect`, `sweep`, or
`rust_source_context`.

Not asset-environment artefacts: the representative failures use fully synthetic
fixtures (`sample_level_visuals`, hand-built traces) with no ROM/asset/global
dependency, and the one asset-touching test reads a fresh, correct-version (v10,
126-level) bundle. These are genuine regressions and brittle tests. The 24
genuinely asset-gated tests are already `#[ignore]`'d and don't run.

Root-cause breakdown (55):

| Cluster | Count | Cause | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `native_player` sprite-frame selection | ~32 | Frame/pose signatures collapse to stuck constants (recurring `Some(18)` = IronKnight `jump_fall`, even for base-form idle) | grandfather → triage |
| `native_player` position/lifecycle "other" | ~10 | Mixed scene-builder regressions (object placement `None`, etc.) | grandfather → triage |
| `native_player` audio-transition | 6 | GEMS BGM-stop sequencing (`StoppedForTransition` vs `Level(..)`/`Start(7)`) | grandfather → triage |
| `native_player` render-pixel | 4 | Priority/reveal pixel diffs | grandfather → triage |
| `inspect` 0x20 block list | 1 | `load_inspect_block_list` returns `None` for later levels despite fresh bundle | grandfather → triage |
| `sweep::frames` demo-return latch | 1 | Pinned frame SHA1 drifted (render change never re-baselined) | cheap fix (verify-tas-full first) |
| `rust_source_context` | 1 | Brittle hardcoded line numbers into `blocks.rs` (grew to 7941 lines) | cheap fix |

Strategy: gate first, then triage. `scripts/failing_test_ratchet.py` +
`docs/source-port/failing-test-baseline.yaml` pin the named failure set at a
downward-only baseline (wired as the hk `failing-test-ratchet` step, mirroring
`dead-code-ratchet`; a new failure outside the set blocks the commit, a fix
`--update`-shrinks the baseline). The two cheap fixes land immediately
(`rust_source_context` de-brittled to content lookups; `sweep::frames`
re-baselined only after a green `verify-tas-full` confirms the current native
render at frame 1837 is gate-accepted, since that frame is inside the
`any-percent-published` `--compare-pixels` range 0..37759 feeding
`tas-pixel-baseline`), shrinking the baseline to 53.

The remaining 53 (52 `native_player` + 1 `inspect`) are deferred triage: each
cluster needs a test-vs-production verdict. Some may be tests written ahead of
implementation → `#[ignore]` with a re-derivation note per AGENTS.md; others are
real engine-level regressions to fix (bsnes rule: fix at engine level, never
per-level). Remove a test from the baseline in the same commit that fixes it.

Evidence source: `cargo test -p wildside-cli` on clean `main` (authoritative for
test status). Native repro: reproduced. Minimum gate: `failing-test-ratchet` +
`verify-slice-fast`.

The earlier diagnosis of a missed decoder bank-wait boundary was incomplete.
All 68000 source-instruction starts match oracle, and native/oracle public
GEMS state remains exact through the decoder RTS at 9,251,741. The first
hidden difference instead occurs during the preceding transfer at cycle
9,161,735: GEMS `LD A,($076D); SUB 1` at `$07B0..$07B4`, with A=0, produces
AF `$FFBB` natively versus `$FF93` in jgenesis. The MIT `z80` core follows
real undocumented Z80 behaviour by copying X/Y from result bits 5/3.
jgenesis `cpu/z80-emu/src/core/instructions/arithmetic.rs::subtract`
preserves the previous X/Y fields. GEMS later serialises AF through its
stack, so the difference becomes visible at the second transfer boundary
(native PC `$02AE`, oracle `$02AA`) despite exact 68000 timing.
`The Undocumented Z80 Documented` and the Z80 flag-affection reference both
confirm that ordinary `SUB` copies these result bits. This checkpoint is
therefore an evidence-backed oracle limitation, not a native CPU bug. The
previously rejected direct-jgenesis dependency remains rejected for
GPL/licence metadata/advisory reasons, and the hardware-faithful MIT core
must not be patched to imitate this oracle defect.

### #405

Opened and resolved 2026-07-13 during the next proactive confidence audit.
`verify-tas` called its narrow progression checksum simply `CRC`, while two
reclassification comments claimed CRC-clean frames proved rendered or pixel
equality. The implementation and `NativeTraceFrame` documentation contradicted
that claim: the checksum covers 11 player/camera progression fields and excludes
render, audio, enemies, object counts, velocity, and other gameplay state. The
full TAS run produces oracle PNGs but no corresponding native full-route PNG
stream, so it cannot compare every rendered frame.

Reports now publish a named `player_camera_progression_v1` projection with the
exact field list and explicit `proves_pixels=false` / `proves_whole_state=false`
flags. Both `verify-tas-frontier` and `verify-tas-full` ratchet this contract.
CLI and gate output says `player/camera CRC`, and the full gate explicitly states
that no full-route pixel comparison is performed. `research-map.md` now records
the current zero-difference typed result without retaining stale intermediate
counts as the current frontier.

The projection unit regression and a 20-frame native/oracle smoke pass, with the
new report contract present. This improves confidence reporting, not pixel
coverage: only the separate named visual gates prove exact source-port pixels at
their stated checkpoints. A future full-route pixel claim requires a bounded
native render stream and exact comparison against the oracle frames.

### #389

branch, and `Enemy0F_UFOBeam_Init` offsets each laser by -4/+4 pixels according
to `x_direction`. Native had independent shooters, consumed random bytes for
an unreachable branch, and centred each beam.

delete it on the first terrain collision instead of reusing the terrain-blind
walking-Dragon breath lifecycle. Exact regressions pin same-frame shooter
serialization, both X-direction offsets, and floor-contact deletion. Level
0x48's fatal frame-42 hit disappears; all 360 player/camera CRC frames match.
Its residual frame-175 HP difference is independently traced to a Drips drop,
not the UFO path.

block resources when available. Regression

the 40x28 grid and frame-60 death, then pins the 20x56 grid plus the oracle's

### #381

Opened 2026-07-11 from #380's residual Level 0x14 idle-tail divergence.
Native allocates two Drips surface crawlers by recording frame 359 against
oracle's three, and the lifecycle split is already present at frame 0.

Investigation 2026-07-11 localised the cause to the recording-warp adapter,
not `Drips.asm` countdown or crawler logic. Oracle hidden-settle tracing shows
the three controllers allocated during the live title-wait shell. At
title-wait step 94, `loc_3340E` has seeded their `d0` waits to `$33/$1F/$3D`;
27 subsequent object passes leave `$18/$04/$22` at `post_title_start` and
`target_live` step 0. RNG is `$FFD1` there, advances exactly one
`Get_RandomNumber_long` per hidden live row, ends step 59 at `$FFE1`, and
reaches `$FFE5` on scenario frame 0.

Native enters `prime_respawn_settle_enemy_loading_loc_368a8` at `$FFD5` and
directly schedules all 32 inspected settle frames through
`step_active_enemies_with_rng`, consuming only the three Drips seed bytes and
leaving `$FFD8` before the stable window. The subsequent window has the correct
four-byte cadence, but it starts from already-wrong waits (`$801E/$18/$00`)
and ring state. ASM `Mode_Level` calls `Execute_Objects`, whose `loc_E12` head
draws `Get_RandomNumber_long` before object coroutines on every live pass; the
collapsed native prime bypasses that ordering.

Rejected: changing the 60-frame window, forcing a third crawler count, or
adding another level-specific RNG ring reset like the existing Level 1 shim.
Those hide the pre-frame state error and violate the engine-level rule. Next:
model the hidden title-wait/respawn prime through one generic Mode_Level frame
scheduler, or preserve a typed pre-frame settle boundary that includes global
RNG and object ordering. Prove it against hidden settle traces for more than
one level before changing #381 gameplay state.

Follow-up 2026-07-11 added full 55-byte RNG-ring capture to hidden settle rows;
offset plus last byte was insufficient to compare collapsed boundaries. Level
0x14 keeps the ring frozen through title-wait step 78, then starts the live
`Execute_Objects` cadence as Load_InGame restores the player and object roster.
The header pose appears across steps 79-80, while native's synthetic settle
step 0 matches step 80. Burning a longword on all 32 synthetic rows therefore
double-counts non-equivalent phases and lands frame 0 at `$FFCA`, not `$FFE5`.

The stronger ring comparison also rejects an offset-only rewind: native enters
the post-resume prime at `$FFD5`, but rewinding one longword does not reproduce
oracle target-live step 0's full `$FFD1` ring. Level 0x05 has a different full
ring and earlier live-load point at the same title-wait step, so one universal
ring constant would merely replace a per-level reset with another hidden
override. Next: schedule enemy loading inside the real level-skip resume/load
phase, using its typed live-load transition rather than replaying floor/camera
inspection rows after the shell has completed.

lifecycle reproduced the oracle's two early object passes, hibernated through
tick 77, and ran hidden `Mode_Level` from tick 78 before the recording settle.
The focused Level 0x14 route reached six objects and RNG offset `$FFE5` at

bug: `loc_123CC` adds byte-valued `Level_width_tiles` directly to `a4`, whereas
native doubled it. The corrected decoder is byte-exact on all 230,440 fixture
cells across 35 non-aliased dumped levels.

groups, 6 teleporters, and 8 hidden records. A synthetic stream exercises all
four families; comparison against 35 dumped RAM sidecars matches every prize
count, and Level 0x13 matches every field across all four self-consistent
sections. Canonical state report `1783729994` improves from 30 pass / 39 fail /
173 authoritative diffs to 33 pass / 36 fail / 150 authoritative diffs, with
Levels 0x29, 0x53, and 0x66 becoming green and advisory diffs unchanged at 5.

unchanged 212-authoritative / 2-oracle-limitation checkpoint baseline.

Opened 2026-07-10 from proactive verification of the whole-level state sweep.

The settle checkpoint is exact, but the idle-tail checkpoint diverges after
native walking-Dragon breath damages Kid one frame early. Framewise comparison
is exact through frame 301; native enters projectile damage at frame 302 while
oracle remains stationary until frame 303. Native repro: yes. Oracle status:
authoritative. Minimum gate: `1p-accurate`.

ASM `Mode_Level` runs `Execute_Objects`, then `GfxObjects_MoveAndAnimate`, then
the Kid-projectile collision passes and `sub_1D76`; `Dragon.asm loc_3D082`
hibernates before polling the live breath child. Native currently advances all
projectiles immediately before testing their new positions for Kid contact in
`resolve_frame_hazards`. Root-cause hypothesis: the native contact pass observes
the Dragon child at its next-frame position. Pin the contact ordering with a
focused regression before changing the shared projectile path.

Resolved 2026-07-10. The initial Dragon-contact diagnosis was false: Level 0
was one hidden settle pass old, so recording frame 0 now supplies the 60th
`loc_1AE2E` live pass. Its full 359-frame player/camera CRC trace then matches
oracle exactly. The wider sweep had two independent infrastructure defects:
state scenarios never enabled recording-oracle settle, and contextual
reclassification replaced evidence-backed oracle limitations with the default
authoritative category. Both now have regressions.

Real checkpoints exposed three pre-existing native bugs. Lion init copied ASM
hitbox words `$48/$4A` into native projectile bookkeeping fields `$5B/$71`,
suppressing roar/fire; those slots now start clear. The Level 0x1B Sphere fix
also made every recording settle require final camera Y before enemy scheduling,
under-ageing Level 0x07's Lion; only the vertical Sphere level keeps that gate.
Finally, logical Level 0x09 maps to resource 0x56 and had no RAM block-list
sidecar. Native decoded its `loc_11C7E` terrain successfully, then discarded the
grid because the sidecar was absent, making Kid fall through the level and
eventually producing the misleading Dragon breath. Decoded terrain now remains
usable with a deliberately empty interactive list; full list synthesis is #378.

parity. The first actionable failure moves to #377 (Level 0x10 object roster).

### #372

Fixed-candidate 2026-07-07: re-read `kid.asm sub_1007A`, `loc_100DA` through
`loc_10120`, and `stru_101B6`. The ROM copies the original prize block art into
GfxObject VRAM slots `$220/$229`, marks the live `Level_Layout` cell `$6F00`,
and draws that copied block as a low-priority GfxObject while the y script moves
it up/down. Native had the right copied block art and `$6Fxx` source-cell
suppression from #324, but queued the prize wobble sprite before Scroll A terrain.
That let later ordinary low-priority tree/background terrain overwrite the
shifted copied block after priority had already been resolved, producing the
"disappears instead of wobbling" visual.

Renderer fix: `build_game_scene_filtered` now queues foreground terrain, block-grid
Scroll A overrides, special foreground-plane draws, and EOL foreground reveal
before `push_prize_block_wobble_overrides_sub_1007a`. This keeps the existing
high-priority foreground mask semantics intact: high-priority terrain can still
mask the low-priority sub_1007A sprite, but ordinary low-priority Scroll A art
cannot erase it after the sprite has drawn. Regression
`prize_block_wobble_sprite_stays_over_low_priority_terrain_sub_1007a_issue372`
failed pre-fix with the row-above terrain colour winning and now passes with the
copied prize-block pixel visible. Focused verification:
`cargo test -q -p wildside-frame prize_block_wobble -- --nocapture` and
`cargo test -q -p wildside-frame scene_pixel_provenance_tracks_priority_acceptance_and_clear -- --nocapture`
pass; `mise run verify-slice-fast` also passes. Current BLW1 #324 route recaptures are under
`.cache/debug/issue372/blw1-row1-scene-after/`, with oracle comparison frames
under `.cache/debug/issue372/blw1-row1-oracle-current/`.

Follow-up 2026-06-10 for #260 after `8d93c638`: the closer cache-local route
`.cache/debug/issue260-route-probes/floor-explicit-left-drips-close-617.json`
is still rejected as metal-block proof because it diverges at frame 596 on
native-only Drips damage before any block contact, but it now gives a precise
Drips root-cause target. `probe-record-scenario-file --frame-start 0
--frame-end 570 --debug-fields --target-projectile drips-drop` shows the left
Drips layout #07 reseeds at native frame 414 with
`drips_splash_reseed_probe=#07 ... table:0->1 ... kid_x=0x0219
reseed_rng=0x4c wait=0x000a`, then again at frame 490 with
`table:1->2 ... reseed_rng=0x7f wait=0x0009`, so the sentinel/crawler splash
arrives at frame 565 and the startup crawler hurts Kid at frame 596. The
matching oracle roster contradicts hitbox and splash-duration fixes: at frame
409 oracle's left Drips has just returned to `loc_33424` with
`a0=0x00033522` and `d0=0x37`, and at frame 414 it is still counting down at
`d0=0x32`, while native is already waiting only `0x0a`. Reading `Drips.asm
loc_3340E` confirms the wait formula is simply `(rng_byte & $FF) >> 2` with
the low byte of `Addr_GfxObject_Kid.x_pos` XORed in; with Kid at `0x0219`, the
oracle counter implies an initial value around `0x38`, not native's `0x0a`.
So the remaining early-crawler blocker is an RNG stream/order displacement
before the first left Drips post-splash reseed, not `d3` cadence (ASM reads
`off_33520` every splash because `d3` is reset to 1), not `stru_33332` splash
length, and not the `DripsSurfaceCrawler` collision box. Next implementation
target: trace RNG consumers before frame 409/414 in this route, especially
same-frame Drips/controller continuations and any player/enemy object pass that
can consume a ROM random byte before `Drips.asm loc_3340E`.

Note 2026-06-03 for #147: narrowed the shared root cause to the
floor-collision-during-cling re-stick at `crates/kid-core/src/movement.rs:3497-3512`.
ASM cross-check confirms the *form selection* is faithful: `loc_AD7C`/`loc_AD98`/
`loc_ADAC` (kid.asm:13581-13599) re-enter the cling loop `loc_AA22` with
`collision_type=4` exactly when `Current_Helmet > 2` (Red Stealth=3, Iron
Knight=6, Berzerker=7 — the three reopened forms), which native mirrors with
`form.helmet_id() > 2`. The single-cell overhang release
`try_release_wall_cling_overhang` (`movement.rs:4171`, ASM `loc_AB22`/`sub_AE6E`)
is one-shot and only fires when the wall actually ends, so it is NOT the climb.
The multi-cell "zoom to top" therefore comes from the form RETAINING its jump's
upward velocity each frame while the re-stick keeps `on_ground=false` and re-arms
sticky, so it rises through the stack instead of landing. REMAINING WORK (per the
hard "probe before changing movement code" rule, deferred twice already): add a
non-Kid (Red Stealth) wall-side-jump probe scenario, trace `y_pos`/`y_velocity`
per frame vs oracle to confirm the retained-velocity mechanism and the ROM's
cling-loop vertical handling at `loc_AA22`, THEN gate the re-stick so it does not
keep an ascending form airborne through solid cells. Not fixed this session —
movement physics must not be changed on a hypothesis.

The first concrete mismatch is Wild Side frame 1080: 5,991 changed pixels, bounds x=36..295 y=143..214, matching the playtest "Everybody played it" kids/door corruption. Oracle WRAM at frame 1080 confirms the native roster selection is not the first cause: `$FFFFFC83=1`, active roster 0, 11 gfx objects, with `loc_1AEEC` descriptor positions/frames matching native. This fixes the wall audit state gap: refreshed `.cache/recordings/issue-206-diamond-power-wall-audit` has `trace_match=true` and `oracle_state_match=true`; strict pixels still fail (`oracle_frame_match=false`, first checkpoint `diamond_power_input` changed pixels 4,127) from pre-existing broad Forest background/palette/rendering differences. A surprise in this pass was that the repeated Wall collision could delete a hibernating DragonWalking corpse early; native now keeps `Dragon.asm loc_3CEFC`/`stru_3CCEC` death objects resident and ignores further pending collision words until the shared delete tail runs. Regressions: `kid_projectile_dp_collision_word_loc_1ea0_uses_object_meta_low_byte_table`, `diamond_power_wall_of_death_collision_rect_uses_unk_31dcc_loc_1d84`, `diamond_power_wall_of_death_overlap_loc_1d84_is_inclusive`, `wall_of_death_slot_collision_queues_dragon_kidabove_loc_1d84_1ea0`, `dragon_walking_death_animation_bypasses_live_retention_loc_3cefc`, and `dragon_walking_death_ignores_repeated_pending_collision_loc_3cefc`. Next #206 pass should use the now-state-green Wall audit to isolate Wall sprite/pixel composition, then repeat the same per-slot collision promotion for Circle before Snake/Five-Way.

Note 2026-05-31 for #206: Circle-of-Doom now uses the shared DP-object collision-word path instead of the temporary all-enemy AoE. Native returns each Circle slot's `$1A/$1E` world position from `DiamondPower_Main_CircleOfDoom loc_3F81A`, derives the `$22=$1144+size*4` rectangle used by `sub_1D84`, maps the overlapped object's `$3A&$FF` through `loc_1EA0`/`unk_1EBE`, writes `colid_rightwall` back to the slot status, and queues parent/child collisions through the pending collision system. Tank child collisions now route through `Tank.asm loc_3B464/loc_3B49A` instead of parent-body damage. Regressions: `circle_of_doom_main_does_not_blanket_delete_enemies_loc_3f81a_loc_1d84`, `circle_of_doom_slot_collision_refreshes_roster_loc_3f81a_loc_1d84`, and `circle_of_doom_slot_collision_routes_tank_child_through_loc_3b41c`. Note 2026-05-31 for #206: Snake DP slot traversal now matches the ROM linked-list order. `DiamondPower_Init_Snake loc_3F92A` saves the first allocated object as the head at `$FFFFF5B4`, but `Allocate_DiamondPowerObjectSlot` prepends later slots to `Addr_FirstDPObjectSlot`; `DiamondPower_Main_Snake loc_3F978` therefore updates trail slots until it reaches the saved head, then moves that head at `loc_3FAD4`. Note 2026-05-31 for #212: found and fixed a transform-HP table conflation while tracing the report. ASM `sub_7EB2` seeds `Number_Hitpoints` from `unk_7EC2` (TheKid=2, Skycutter/Cyclone/RedStealth/Eyeclops/Juggernaut=3, IronKnight=$0C, Berzerker=4, Maniaxe=8, Micromax=$10), whereas `Check_for_recent_damge -> loc_B700` and `Make_SpriteAttr_HUD/sub_BDC0` use `HelmetHitpoint_Table` (IronKnight damage/HUD cap 5, most helmets 3). Native had reused `PlayerForm::max_hitpoints()` for transform HP, so IronKnight/Berzerker/Maniaxe/Micromax started too low compared with ROM. `transform_hitpoints_sub_7eb2` now mirrors `unk_7EC2`, with regression `sub_7eb2_uses_transform_hp_table_not_damage_cap_table`; existing `loc_B700` damage tests prove the first damage frame caps oversized IronKnight HP to 5 before subtracting to 4. Follow-up triage closed the live DragonWalking part with `loc_b700_iron_knight_survives_first_dragon_contact_with_four_hp`; the human-visible "first pip does not change" is consistent with the ROM's separate transform HP seed and damage/HUD cap rather than a one-hit form-loss bug.

Note 2026-05-31 for #212: added a cache-local direct contact probe at `.cache/scenarios/issue-212-iron-dragon-contact.json` / `.cache/recordings/issue-212-iron-dragon-contact` using `playtest_form=6`, Level 00, Kid at `(165,271)` against the active DragonWalking object. `verify-tas --scenario .cache/recordings/issue-212-iron-dragon-contact/scenario.json --frame-start 0 --frame-end 20 --checkpoint-interval 1 --frontier-kind gameplay` shows no helmet loss in either runtime. Oracle has `number_hitpoints=5`, `Just_received_damage=false` at frame 0 while the DragonWalking object exposes `collision_type=$28(kidbelow)`, then `Just_received_damage=true` from frame 1 and HP effectively drops to 4. Native applies `ContactDamage` on frame 0 (`number_hitpoints=4`, `Just_received_damage=true`) and clears its public one-frame latch on frame 1. So the direct DragonWalking report narrowed to a one-frame collision handoff / damage-latch timing mismatch, not an instant IronKnight form loss; follow-up focused regression coverage is enough to close this row as "not the reported one-hit helmet loss".

Native already hid Drips controllers in the renderer, but `active_objects` still exported the parent as an enemy snapshot. `rebuild_active_enemy_roster` now keeps Drips parent/controllers internal and exports only visible falling/surface children through projectile snapshots, citing `Drips.asm Enemy16_Drip_Init`/`loc_33488`. Note 2026-05-31 for #213: native was deleting the lower Level 1 Drips falling child when it sat just outside the narrow Lion projectile camera box (`screen_x=$188`). ASM `Drips.asm loc_3345C` calls `Object_CheckInRange` on the hidden controller, not Lion `sub_3E2CE` on the child projectile, so commit `c5c60e19` exempts `EnemyProjectileKind::DripsDrop` from that generic owner cull and adds `drips_drop_loc_3345c_ignores_lion_projectile_camera_box`. Verification: `cargo test -q -p kid-core drips_drop_loc_3345c_ignores_lion_projectile_camera_box -- --nocapture`, `mise run verify-slice-fast`, and `tas-diff --scenario .cache/scenarios/issue-213-drips-floor-probe-2000.json --frame-start 520 --frame-end 620 --frontier-kind enemy --include-advisory --only-divergent`. Important rejected hypothesis: do not count every active Drips controller or every native Drips drop in `Number_Objects`; that overcounts frames 520-536. Oracle WRAM reports the count-visible child window at frames 537-597, while native still schedules the simplified drop cycles at 73/157/263/340/454/555, so the remaining root cause is the Drips animation/timing child-slot model, not the projectile cull.

Note 2026-05-31 for #213: commit `147c296c` implemented the first part of the remaining Drips child-slot model. ASM `Drips.asm loc_33424` waits through `stru_33F90` (`$A,$A,8,6,1` frames) before setting `$13/$14/$3C(a1)` and exposing the falling child; native had spawned `DripsDrop` immediately on timer expiry. Regression `drips_drop_uses_dedicated_child_slot_not_generic_projectile_cap_loc_33424` now proves the forming animation delay before the child bypasses the generic projectile cap. Verification: `cargo test -q -p kid-core drips_ -- --nocapture`, `mise run verify-slice-fast`, and the same lower-floor `tas-diff` window. Follow-up rejected hypothesis: simply adding pre-drop Drips animations to `gameplay_transient_gfx_worker_count` makes the lower-floor probe worse (21 match / 79 diverge) by overcounting native after oracle drops back to 5 at frame 598. The remaining mismatch is a precise timing/window alignment problem, not just missing trace projection for pre-drop workers.

### 001 — Player stuck after damage (FIXED)
Root cause: `apply_damage()` did not clear `left_wall_sticky` / `right_wall_sticky`.
If the player was wall-grabbed when hit, they stayed pinned to the wall during
invulnerability frames. Fix: clear both wall-sticky fields in `apply_damage()`.

### 002 — Enemies don't die when stomped (FIXED)
Root cause: stomp detection used strict `previous_bottom <= stomp_e_top` position check,
requiring the player's feet to be precisely above the enemy's top edge on the prior frame.
The ASM uses a velocity-direction cross-product: `y_overlap × |rel_x_vel| < x_overlap × |rel_y_vel|`
to determine approach direction. Reimplemented to match ASM — stomps are now detected based
on vertical approach direction, not prior-frame position history.

### 122 — Level 2 entry can spawn Kid in midair, then fall through the floor and die (FIXED)
Evidence source: repeated native play reports plus strengthened native smoke coverage.
Native repro: the old `progress-two-transitions` gate never actually resumed Level 2 gameplay.
Oracle repro: unknown. Minimum gate: `1p-playable`.

Fix: extend `progress-two-transitions` so it re-arms the second skip hold on frame `2700`,
records `level_2_settle@2701`, and then survives through `level_2_live_tail@3300`. The native
gate now proves stable Level 2 landing plus 10 seconds of live gameplay instead of stopping in
`game_mode=$0008` transition mode.

Surprise worth keeping: the real Blue Lake Woods 2 header spawn is intentionally midair at
`(32,160)`, and the hidden `Load_InGame` settle path was already landing safely. The real gap was
the smoke scenario: it ended before sending the second resume input, so we were treating a
transition-shell check as if it proved live Level 2 play.

### 123 — Death/respawn still leaves camera drift, stuck-from-start, or broken restart state (FIXED)
Evidence source: repeated native play reports. Native repro: reported, needs canonical recording slug.
Oracle repro: mixed/unknown. Minimum gate: `1p-playable`.

This issue stays separate from the closed floor-snap and TAS frontier items. It is a player-facing
native stability bug until a recording or focused scenario proves otherwise.

Latest evidence: the old gameplay compare drift at `level_settle@719` was partly a stale native
opening-hazard model, not just a bad checkpoint. Oracle-backed Level 1 gameplay can take an idle
opening dragon hit on frame `631` and the fatal follow-up on frame `698`; native now mirrors those
two hits and enters `DeathWindup`, and the widened `progress-two-transitions` scenario now passes
its oracle compare again. `death-respawn-level1` is still open: after starting that smoke path
earlier to dodge the idle-hazard window, the first compare miss is now a narrower camera-X drift at
`level_settle@719` (native `0x00AA0000`, oracle `0x00800000`). The remaining work is the respawn
shell camera hand-off, not the opening hit timing itself.

New evidence: death/continue restart was also leaking stale per-level runtime state. Native now
rebuilds the current-level respawn shell with a clean object/effect/weather/camera-look state:
`killed_enemies`, projectiles, transient block/effect lists, murder wall/weather state, helmet
ability state, Diamond Power state, and `y_look_offset` all reset before `Respawning` begins.
Focused regressions `death_respawn_restarts_with_clean_level_runtime_state` and
`continue_respawn_restarts_with_clean_level_runtime_state` lock this down. The `pause_resume_level1`
and `death_respawn_level1` smoke scripts now reuse the oracle-backed walk-only opening baseline
before layering pause / death input, so `mise run verify-1p-playable` is green again. The oracle
compare is still open, but the stale setup-window misses are gone: `pause-resume-level1` now first
misses later at `resumed_tail@1119` (`camera_x` native `0x028E0000`, oracle `0x02AF0000`), and
`death-respawn-level1` now first misses later at `pre_death@1279` (`hp` native `0`, oracle `1`).
The remaining work is still the respawn/camera hand-off, not the smoke setup itself.

### 137 — Kid walks backwards while climbing slopes (FIXED)
2026-04-25 fix: `update_level_one_slope_ground_velocity` in `crates/kid-core/src/movement.rs` inverted the slope-flag → `Direction` translation in all three branches (uphill `loc_9DC0`, downhill `loc_9DF2`, neutral `loc_9E4C`). The ASM stores the slope-flag byte (`$FFFFFA26`: 0 for SlopeUp, $FF for SlopeDown) — possibly XOR-flipped — into `x_direction(a3)`, and Kid's default-right sprite means `x_direction=0`→Right while `x_direction=$FF`→Left. Native returned the opposite Direction in every case, so holding Right uphill on SlopeUp rendered Left (the moonwalk repro the user reported). Detection that flagged it: the walk_right gameplay assertion added in `082b0437` (`kid_facing_matches_input` self-consistency check) lights the divergence up across all 105 sweep levels without needing the oracle. New unit test `slope_facing_does_not_invert_on_uphill_traversal_loc_9DC0` exhaustively pins all 8 ASM-derived facing cases (uphill/downhill/neutral × SlopeUp/SlopeDown, plus the canonical-vel sign flip in the neutral branch), and four existing slope-walk tests that had locked in the buggy facing were updated to assert the ASM-correct value alongside the velocity check they already covered. The fix is engine-level; no per-helmet or per-level overrides were needed (special forms — Eyeclops/RedStealth/Maniaxe — already used a separate path at `loc_9E6C` that was correct).

2026-05-29 follow-up: fresh playtest reported a visual-only regression when Kid moves back down the first Level 00 slope. Root cause: native had fixed the gameplay-facing branch but still left the slope sprite phase as a renderer approximation (`frame_index / 4`) for non-Juggernaut forms, while ASM `loc_A13A -> loc_A172 -> loc_A17E` advances and indexes `$FFFFF8F0` for every slope form. Native now models `slope_walk_visual_accumulator_loc_A13A` in the grounded slope motion path and the renderer consumes `walk_visual_accumulator >> 8` for Kid slope frames. Regressions: `loc_a13a_slope_walk_visual_accumulator_uses_direction_and_run_state`, `kid_slope_frame_phase_uses_walk_visual_accumulator_loc_a13a`.

2026-05-25 playtest follow-up: the remaining top-left→bottom-right slope complaint was visual descriptor drift, not a new slope-facing state bug. ASM `loc_A13A` correctly selects the `kid_slope_7..12` bank for the SlopeDown/right-facing canonical path, but native had lost the signed negative Y origins from `unk_A2552`, `unk_A26D8`, `unk_A29E4`, and `unk_A2B6A`. Those frames now keep their ROM `-$02`/`-$01` origins so the SlopeDown bank aligns with the diagonal instead of looking like the wrong/half-flipped sprite.

### 126 — Walking up slopes is still observably wrong in native play (FIXED)
Evidence source: repeated native play reports plus ASM audit. Native repro: focused physics divergence reproduced in tests.
Oracle repro: ASM-backed via `loc_9D22`, `unk_9EB0`, `unk_9EE4`, and `loc_9E6C`. Minimum gate: `1p-playable`.

Root cause: native only applied the ROM slope-velocity helper to `TheKid`. That left
Skycutter/Cyclone/Juggernaut/IronKnight/Berzerker falling back to flat-ground acceleration
while still using slope Y-snapping, and left Red Stealth/Eyeclops/Maniaxe missing their
separate fixed-step slope branch entirely.

Fix landed: `update_level_one_slope_ground_velocity()` now mirrors the three ROM families:
shared `unk_9EB0` tables for the main helmets, `unk_9EE4` for Micromax, and the
input-agnostic `loc_9E6C` branch for Red Stealth/Eyeclops/Maniaxe. Regressions:
`slope_ground_run_right_uses_shared_table_for_cyclone` and
`slope_ground_special_form_auto_slides_without_input`.

Closure evidence: `mise run verify-1p-playable` now keeps the existing slope-family
unit coverage and also exercises uphill/downhill tracking plus slope enter/exit seam
regressions via `walking_on_slope_up_y_tracks_diagonal_every_frame`,
`walking_on_slope_down_y_tracks_diagonal_every_frame`,
`solid_to_slope_up_transition_stays_grounded`, and
`grounded_slope_to_solid_seam_keeps_level_one_runner_grounded`.

stub rather than the ROM menu. Oracle repro: ASM-backed. Minimum gate: `fast-slice`.

Root cause: the native title/options flow had grown a convenient stub menu and we had implicitly
treated "password flow" as a missing feature without first checking the stock ROM path.

Fix: re-read `kid.asm` `Title_InputLoop` and `OptionScreen_Input`. The stock game exposes
`1 PLAYER / 2 PLAYERS / OPTIONS` on the title screen, then a four-row options screen:
`2 PLAYERS`, `CONTROLS`, `SPEED BUTTON`, and `EXIT`. There is no password entry in the stock ROM
path. Native now mirrors that menu structure, stores the ROM-backed option state
(`Options_Suboption_2PController`, `Options_Suboption_Controls`, `Options_Suboption_Speed`), and
updates the native player options scene accordingly.

Surprise worth keeping: the earlier native `Sound Test` submenu was a project-local convenience,
not a stock-ROM behaviour. The right fix for the backlog item was to document "no password flow in
the shipped ROM" and align native options with the actual disassembly instead of inventing another
menu branch.

### 142 — Level 1 dragon breath travels too far (FIXED)
ASM audit 2026-04-05: `loc_3D02A` spawns breath as a stationary GfxObject (animation `stru_3CCC8`, 68 frames: 8+10+10+10+10+10+10) placed at ±28px (`DRAGON_WALKING_BREATH_OFFSET_PX`). Native incorrectly created a travelling projectile with `x_velocity=0x30000` and `lifetime=68`, covering 204px. Fix: zero velocity, keep lifetime=68 (matches animation duration). Also fixed flying dragon fire (`loc_34BAC`): added ±10px X offset and `terrain_kill` (ASM uses off-screen `$19(a3)` cull, not frame timer).

### 144 — Level 2 shooter enemy fires too rapidly (EVIDENCE NEEDED)
ASM audit 2026-04-05: Root cause was **enemy ID mapping**. ASM has two distinct types:
- `0x0A` = `Enemy0A_RockTank_Init` (Tank.asm) — paces, opens/closes mouth, **never fires**
- `0x0B` = `Enemy0B_RockTank_shooting_Init` (Tank_Shooting.asm) — fires via animation-driven trigger

Native used to map 0x0A→`EnemyFamily::Tank` (erroneously fired every 32 frames) and 0x0B→`Unknown(0x0B)/Inert` (not spawned at all). Level 2 has 4 type-0x0B enemies that should be shooting but were invisible.

ASM fire cadence: animation-driven via `sub_3C4F8` checking turret anim mapping == `LnkTo_unk_C7F10` AND `$32(a4)==5`. HP≥4: 116 frames/shot (`stru_3B4D8`). HP<4: 232 frames/shot (`stru_3B4F6`). Native: 32 frames/shot → 3.6–7.25x too fast.

Fix landed:
1. Added `EnemyFamily::TankShooting` for enemy ID `0x0B`
2. Removed projectile fire from plain `EnemyFamily::Tank`
3. Wired the shooter cadence to ASM `sub_3C4F8` / `loc_3C50E` with the `stru_3B4D8` / `stru_3B4F6` frame timing
4. Corrected bullet spawn offset to ±15px X and turret_y-14 Y per `loc_3B730`

Regression coverage:
- `tank_shooting_layout_object_maps_enemy_id_0b`
- `tank_shooting_fire_uses_loc_3c50e_cadence_and_loc_3b730_offsets`
- `tank_shooting_spawn_wait_timer_matches_first_loc_3c50e_fire_gate`

### 145 — Level 2 shooter enemy rendered incorrectly (EVIDENCE NEEDED)
ASM audit 2026-04-05: Tank uses **2 GfxObject slots** (body at `a3`, turret at `$3A(a5)`). Native uses 1 sprite. Missing turret has independent animations:
- Non-shooting (`stru_3B27E`): 5-frame mouth open/close, 92 frames
- Shooting HP≥4 (`stru_3B4D8`): 7-frame fire cycle, 116 frames
- Shooting HP<4 (`stru_3B4F6`): 8-frame fire cycle, 232 frames
- Turret offset: body y_pos - 8px, copied via `sub_3BF72` every frame

Fix landed:
1. Native player now emits a second RockTank sprite for the turret child GfxObject instead of collapsing everything into the body sprite.
2. Plain tanks use `stru_3B27E`; shooting tanks use `stru_3B4D8` at HP 4 and `stru_3B4F6` at HP 2-3, reusing the ROM frame descriptors `unk_C7EC8`, `unk_C7F00`, `unk_C7F08`, `unk_C7F10`, `unk_C7F20`, and `unk_C7F28`.
3. The turret render keeps the ROM's y-8px child attachment from `Enemy0A_RockTank_Init` / `Enemy0B_RockTank_shooting_Init`.
4. Follow-up 2026-05-20: the runtime trace already contains both body and child snapshots, so native rendering now draws the body from the HP-bearing parent snapshot and the turret from the HP-less child snapshot instead of synthesising a duplicate turret for both objects. This reduced Level 0x01 full-frame worst mismatch from 7,177 pixels / MAE 4.4 to 6,695 pixels / MAE 3.9 in `cargo run -q -p kidcli -- sweep --levels 1 --tier full --max-failures 1`.

Regression coverage:
- `rock_tank_renderer_emits_body_and_turret_sprites_per_stru_3b27e`
- `rock_tank_shooting_renderer_uses_stru_3b4d8_turret_frames`
- `rock_tank_renderer_uses_child_snapshot_instead_of_duplicate_synthetic_turret`

### 132 — Verify 2-player alternating mode against oracle-backed or strong native scenarios (FIXED)
Evidence source: backlog triage after the 1P gates stabilised. Native repro: existing behaviour, but only partially covered by tests.
Oracle repro: not required — this closure uses strong native scenarios. Minimum gate: `fast-slice`.

Fix: extend the 2P regression coverage in `kid-core` so the alternation rules are explicit:
game over enters `ContinueCountdown` before any player swap, using a continue respawns the
same player without disturbing the other slot, and letting the continue countdown expire
returns to title instead of silently swapping players.

Closure evidence: `cargo test -q -p kid-core two_player_ -- --nocapture` passes with the new
`two_player_game_over_prefers_continue_countdown_before_switching_players`,
`two_player_continue_input_respawns_same_player_and_preserves_other_slot`, and
`two_player_continue_timeout_returns_to_title_without_switching_players` regressions, and
`mise run verify-slice-fast` stays green.

### 124 — Enemy kill timing still allows Kid to get hurt after the enemy should already be dead (FIXED)
Evidence source: native play reports. Native repro: reported, not yet captured.
Oracle repro: unknown. Minimum gate: `fast-slice`.

Root cause: non-stomp kill paths removed the live enemy object, but only stomps updated the
layout-backed `killed_enemies` bitfield. The next activation pass could therefore recreate a
"dead" enemy from the layout while its spawn remained in the active window, which made the
contact damage feel one frame late or outright wrong in live play.

Fix: centralised enemy removal so stomps, sword kills, friendly projectiles, Berzerker charge,
and diamond-power AoE all share the same kill bookkeeping and death side-effects. Regression:
`red_stealth_sword_kill_marks_layout_enemy_dead` proves a sword-killed layout enemy no longer
reactivates on the next activation pass.

### 125 — Breakable blocks can render with the wrong lifecycle art or regress into prize-like visuals (FIXED)
Evidence source: code-path audit plus failing render regressions. Native repro: reproduced in tests.
Oracle repro: n/a for this render mapping bug. Minimum gate: `fast-slice`.

Root cause: `kid-render`'s `BlockVisualMapping::resolve()` was treating the decoded
`Block_Mappings` table as skin-only, even though the asset contains five 16-skin
visual groups (smash, prize, ice, metal, rubber) after the terrain entry. That made
cells such as the post-prize `$E001` smash block reuse the prize-family art for the
same skin byte.

Fix: index block visuals by both block family and skin. Regressions:
`load_block_visual_mapping_from_skin_and_block_type`,
`build_game_scene_emits_block_family_tiles_from_skin_and_block_type`, and
`prize_block_lifecycle_restores_smash_family_art_after_dispatch`.

### 127 — Black bouncy blocks do not produce the expected bounce behaviour (FIXED)
Evidence source: backlog follow-up plus ASM review. Native repro: reproduced in code paths.
Oracle repro: ASM-backed via `sub_902A`, `sub_914A`, `sub_8F26`, `sub_922C`, and `loc_10DA4`.
Minimum gate: `fast-slice`.

Root cause: native treated rubber blocks like ordinary solids on contact, so the ROM's
contact-triggered jiggle effect never appeared on landings, head bonks, or wall hits.
The earlier "bounce block" description was misleading: ASM `loc_10DA4` only plays
`sfx_Rubber_block` and spawns the temporary jiggle object; it does not relaunch Kid.

Fix: route rubber floor, ceiling, and wall contacts through the existing block-bounce
visual channel while keeping the ROM-faithful landing and collision velocities intact.
Regressions: `rubber_block_landing_queues_jiggle_without_bouncing_player`,
`rubber_block_ceiling_hit_queues_jiggle_without_destroying_cell`, and
`rubber_block_wall_hit_queues_jiggle_without_breaking_wall`.

### 128 — Form-specific block breaking can now destroy metal blocks that should stay solid (FIXED)
Evidence source: code-path audit after the Iron Knight landing shortcut. Native repro: reproduced in tests.
Oracle repro: ASM-backed via `sub_AF7A`, `off_AFD8`, and `loc_110D0/sub_11120`. Minimum gate: `fast-slice`.

Root cause: native had collapsed Iron Knight's landing block-break dispatch into
"delete every block type `0..5`". The ROM does not do that. `off_AFD8` sends
Smash/Prize/Ice to destructive handlers, SolidGhost/Teleporter to a no-op path,
and Metal to `loc_110D0`, which plays the steel bounce animation and restores
`$E50B` instead of clearing the cell.

Fix: restore that block-type dispatch in the landing path. Regression:
`iron_knight_landing_on_metal_block_bounces_without_destroying_it` proves a
landing Iron Knight now bounces off a metal block, leaves the cell intact, and
queues the steel bounce effect instead of deleting the tile.

### 130 — Turn recordings into the standard playtest evidence pipeline (FIXED)
Evidence source: existing `play-native --record` / `verify-recording` support plus current workflow gaps.
Native repro: partial. Oracle repro: partial. Minimum gate: n/a.

The repo already records input + trace. The missing work is packaging, remote-ingest workflow,
optional artefacts, and making the recording slug the normal reproduction handle for future bugs.

Progress landed: new recording bundles now persist ROM SHA-1, script/trace hashes, host OS/arch,
best-effort git commit/dirty state, and explicit record/verify commands in `manifest.json`, plus
a human-readable `README.txt` so a copied slug is self-describing before verification runs.

Latest progress (2026-03-27): legacy `trace.json` bundles now deserialize through the current
`NativeTraceFrame` schema again. `kid-core` `NativeTraceFrame` now supplies serde defaults for
newer fields, and `kidcli` regression coverage locks a real legacy trace example so
`load_recording()` backfills both manifest metadata and missing trace keys.

Latest progress (2026-03-28): `kidcli verify-recording` now accepts either a local cache slug
(`--slug <slug>`) or a copied bundle path (`--bundle <path>`). That removes the old manual
re-ingest step for remote repro bundles and makes the bundle itself a valid verification handle.

Latest progress (2026-03-28, artefact sidecars): `kidcli play-native --record <slug>` now saves
bundle-level `final-frame.png` and `audio.wav`, and `--record-notes <path>` copies plain-text
player notes into `notes.txt`. The saved `manifest.json` lists those sidecars explicitly so copied
bundles stay self-describing before any replay or oracle verification runs.

Closure evidence (2026-03-28, transcript sidecar): recording bundles now always include an
automatic `transcript.txt` generated from the captured native trace. The transcript logs the start
state plus major event boundaries such as game-mode swaps, level changes, pause toggles, life/HP
changes, helmet swaps, damage latches, game-over entry, and continue countdown updates, so a copied
bundle is reviewable before replaying it. `manifest.json` and `README.txt` now list the transcript
alongside `notes.txt`, `final-frame.png`, and `audio.wav`, and `kidcli` regression coverage locks
the new bundle contract. With transcript sidecars landed, the recording slug is now a complete,
self-describing repro handle rather than just "trace plus optional notes".

### 004 — Palette (FIXED)
Root cause: theme-specific palette permutation tables were not applied. The ASM art
decompression remaps palette indices per theme (Forest, City, Mountain have unique tables).
Fix: load 16-byte permutation tables and reorder palette entries during level visual loading.

### 005 — Parallax (NOT A BUG)
Parallax IS working. bgscroll data loads correctly, `background_scroll_x_px()` applies
camera-relative rates. Effect is subtle (e.g. Forest: 26% camera speed) matching original.

### 006 — Dragon moonwalking (FIXED)
Root cause: `select_enemy_frame` used global `trace.frame_index` for ALL enemies,
cycling walk frames even when the dragon is in a stationary phase (perch/parked).
Fix: added `stationary` field to NativeObjectSnapshot, populated from
`DragonMotionPhase::is_stationary()`. Stationary enemies show frame 0 (idle).

### 038 — Camera Y settling dead-zone (FIXED)
8 levels showed +1 to +7px camera_y diffs at level_settle. The asymmetric dead-zone
in `update_camera_axis` (`(target-camera+4)>>3` rounds to 0 within ±4px) meant the
final camera position depended on approach direction. Floor-snap placed the player
instantly at the floor, so the camera approached from a different direction than the
oracle (which tracks the player frame-by-frame during real gravity fall).
Fix: simulate gravity fall + camera follow in `level_respawn_slice_with_floor_snap` —
replay the player falling from header_y to floor_y under gravity, updating the camera
each step. This matches the oracle's convergence path. Fixed all 8 levels.

### 082 — Demo byte boundary parity shift after transform (FIXED)
On the first Kid_Transform frame, step_demo_input sees form_change_flash_frames=0
(step_lifecycle hasn't set it yet) and advances both counter and data_index. The
data_index advance is correct — it aligns native's data_index with the oracle's
pointer (compensating for the 1-frame late demo start). But the counter advance
shifts the byte-advancement parity for all subsequent frames.

The inverted parity (`playback_frame % 2 == 1` vs oracle's even counter) compensates
for the 1-frame late start during normal play. The extra counter increment on the
first transform frame disrupts this compensation, causing byte boundaries to land
on the wrong frame of each 2-frame window.

Fix: after step_lifecycle (inside refresh_opening_slice), detect when
form_change_flash_frames transitions from >0 to 0 (transform end) and decrement the
counter by 1 to restore the pre-transform parity. Uses `demo_transform_active` bool
to track whether a transform is in progress.

### 091 — Demo Start abort timing (FIXED)
The imported Any% TAS presses real Start on global frame 1772 while demo 0x1B is
still running. Native was handling that input immediately inside `step_demo_input`,
returning to title on the same frame. ASM `loc_119D8` does not do that: it clears
`Ctrl_Pressed`, hibernates for one frame, then checks `Ctrl_1_Pressed` on wake-up.
That makes the visible title transition land two frames after the live Start press.

Fix: add a dedicated deferred demo-title-return countdown in `NativeRuntime`.
Frame 1772 now arms the abort, frame 1773 still stays in `DemoPlay`, and frame 1774
finally calls the title-return cleanup and clears `Current_LevelID` to 0.

oracle therefore spends the first post-abort title phase with `mode=$002C` and

Native was clearing `opening_slice` and reusing the cold-boot title pose as soon
as the abort countdown expired, which skipped that paused handoff phase.

Fix: preserve the demo gameplay snapshot on the title-return path, mark the
runtime paused, and let trace output reuse the preserved Kid/camera snapshot
while title mode is active. Added `demo_title_return_keeps_live_snapshot_on_first_title_frames`
to lock down frames 1774 and 1779.

Attempted approaches that didn't work:
- pending_form.is_some() check: over-freezes (73 vs 72 frames), regression to 1129
- Full deferred pipeline (move step_demo_input after physics): changes byte for ALL frames
  due to 1-frame delay, regression to 921
- Rollback counter+data_index on first transform frame: data_index rollback misaligns
  with oracle (oracle's pointer is 1 ahead due to earlier start), regression to 1129
- Frozen input override (save pre-transform byte for first post-transform physics):
  correct in theory but native already has the right byte via the "compensating"
  data_index advance; freezing gives the WRONG byte, regression to 1129

Key insight: the extra data_index advance on K+1 is a happy accident that aligns
native's data_index with the oracle's. Only the PARITY needs correcting, not the
data_index itself.

### 083 — Demo byte boundary systematic offset (INVESTIGATED)
ASM VBlank pipeline: MainGameLoop → mode handler → Execute_Objects → player
processing → ReadJoypad (loc_C22 demo path). ReadJoypad runs AFTER game logic,
so byte read on frame N is used by game logic on frame N+1. V_Int handler is
minimal (just increments counter + sets done flag), does NOT read joypads.

Oracle probe confirmed: at frame 915, oracle counter (post-ReadJoypad) = 16,
native playback_frame = 14. Oracle counter is consistently 1 ahead of native pf.
Data pointer advances align when using parity `% 2 == 0` (matching oracle's
even-d7 advance pattern).

Attempted pipeline buffer approach:
1. Added `demo_buffered_input: Option<FrameInput>` — return previous frame's byte
2. Changed advancement parity from `% 2 == 1` to `% 2 == 0`
3. Transform compensation: `fc += 1`, `di += 1` at transform end

Result: produces IDENTICAL frontier (frame 1170) with identical position/velocity.
The buffer+parity change is mathematically equivalent to the old code: both have a
net 1-frame offset, just manifested at different parity phases. Changing parity
shifts which frames see the boundary mismatch, but the underlying 1-frame late
start means one boundary per byte pair will always be off.

Why simple compensations fail: native starts demo byte consumption 1 frame after
oracle (confirmed by probe). Adding a pipeline buffer delays usage by 1 frame
(matching ASM's read-after-use), but the late start means the read itself is on
the wrong frame. The parity change fixes the data_index alignment but the buffer
delay cancels out, leaving the same net offset. Any combination of (buffer ×
parity × transform_correction) that produces correct post-transform alignment
also produces the same pre-transform byte boundary behaviour as the old code.

True fix requires: making native start demo byte consumption on the same frame
as the oracle (i.e., fixing the 1-frame start offset), likely by restructuring
how BootState::DemoPlay initialises the counter relative to the ASM's first
ReadJoypad call in demo mode.

### #1

- [rejected_hypotheses] {"name": "Advisory `number_hitpoints` had to stay masked because oracle idle warps always pause and that pause is structural", "reason": "Promoted 2026-05-02. The legacy mask was added in commit 565fc16e back when `classify_state_diff` had no oracle-paused supersedence — it was a blunt workaround for Start-press carryover pausing the oracle on idle warps. Sweep `1777685763` carried 13 advisory `number_hitpoints` diffs across 13 idle scenarios (levels 0x08, 0x09, 0x19, 0x21, 0x32, 0x33, 0x50, 0x56, 0x58, 0x60, 0x61, 0x62, 0x63 at `idle_tail`/`level_settle`). Every single one sat on a checkpoint that already classified `game_paused`, `current_level_id`, `camera_y_pos`, `kid_x_pos`, `kid_y_pos` etc. as `oracle_limitation` — i.e. the oracle was paused by `game_paused=true` and could never reach the ROM damage path at `loc_B722` kid.asm:14646-14658 (`subq.w #1,(Number_Hitpoints).w`) to spend HP, while native ran live and took hits, leaving native HP < oracle HP=2 (the value the ROM seeds via `lose_life` kid.asm:14768 `move.w #2,(Number_Hitpoints).w`). With the precedence reorder from commit 404996c4 (oracle-paused supersedes death-gap) already in place, the field-level mask was redundant: removing `number_hitpoints` from `ADVISORY_FIELDS` lets the same diffs naturally reclassify to `OracleLimitation` while letting any future non-paused HP divergence surface as a real native damage bug rather than being silently swallowed."}
- [rejected_hypotheses] {"name": "Advisory `number_lives` had to stay masked because oracle idle warps always pause and the death path is unreachable", "reason": "Promoted 2026-05-02. Same architectural pattern as `number_hitpoints` — the legacy mask predated the oracle-paused supersedence in `classify_state_diff` and was a blunt workaround for Start-press carryover pausing the oracle on idle warps. Sweep `1777686359` carried 8 advisory `number_lives` diffs (levels 0x09, 0x32, 0x33, 0x48, 0x50, 0x57, 0x61, 0x63 at `idle_tail`), every one with `native=2 oracle=3` on a checkpoint where `game_paused:false->true` was already `oracle_limitation` and `current_level_id` showed the oracle stuck on title (0x0000). The ROM only decrements `Number_Lives` inside the live `lose_life` death path at kid.asm:14766 (`subq.w #1,(Number_Lives).w`); the title-card seed at kid.asm:16568 (`move.w #3,(Number_Lives).w`) is what the paused oracle reports. Native ran live, died once during the idle scenario (lives 3→2), oracle never reached gameplay so it stayed at the seed of 3. With commit 404996c4's precedence reorder, removing `number_lives` from `ADVISORY_FIELDS` lets these diffs naturally reclassify to `OracleLimitation` while letting any future non-paused life-loss divergence surface as a real native bug rather than being silently swallowed."}

(2) Thrust checked C held state; ASM sub_B168 uses `bclr #Button_C,(Ctrl_Pressed)` — rising edge only, one frame of thrust per C press. (3) Edge detection used prior_input (2-frame gap); ASM uses Ctrl_Pressed vs Ctrl_1_Held (1-frame gap). Fix: split into step_cyclone_flight (velocity modulation when already flying) + step_cyclone_activation (after physics, only when not flying). Frontier 1209→1301

### #85

- [Verify] ASM `subi.w`/`addi.w` uses M68K modular 16-bit arithmetic. Native used `saturating_add/sub` which clamps at i16::MIN instead of wrapping. When accumulator gets very negative (~-22016) and thrust (-$3000) is applied, ASM wraps to positive (0xAA00-0x3000=0x7A00=+31232), producing a sudden downward push. Native saturated at -32768. Fix: wrapping_add/wrapping_sub. Frontier 1301→1365

### #138

- [Summary] Enemy contact appears to apply double damage because invulnerability is too short
- [Verify] Validated 2026-05-18 from bounded native bundle `.cache/recordings/issue-138-enemy-contact/`: `cargo run -p kidcli -- verify-recording --slug issue-138-enemy-contact --native-only` passes with `trace_match=true`, `native_replay_only=true`, and 1800 recorded/replayed frames. The transcript reaches settled Level 00 enemy contact and records damage at frames 290 and 356, exactly 66 frames apart, then Kid dies and enters `LevelTransition` on frame 431. This is ROM-faithful behaviour, not native double damage: `GfxObjects_CollisionKid_Collide` / `loc_1D00` suppress damaging collision while `KidIsInvulnerable`; `Check_for_recent_damge` (kid.asm:14632) returns immediately when `Just_received_damage` is set, otherwise falls through to `loc_B700` (kid.asm:14638) which deducts HP and re-arms the latch; `loc_BC34` spawns the damage-flash thread; `loc_BC54` / `loc_BC56` / `loc_BC5C` / `loc_BC6E` (kid.asm:15196..15213) hibernate 11 outer cycles × (2 white + 4 normal) = 66 frames before `sf (Just_received_damage).w` clears the latch. Oracle-parity result: `cargo run -p kidcli -- compare-native-oracle --scenario boot-title-start-level1` passes. Proposed-fix commit: `e6b27bb7bcffd20e410c73573ea3bcebbb549399` (`Fix combat mechanics to match ASM: no knockback, 66-frame invuln`) shrank `PLAYER_DAMAGE_INVULNERABLE_FRAMES` from 300 to 66 (`crates/kid-core/src/constants.rs:393`) and removed invented knockback velocities. Regression `enemy_contact_double_damage_gate_releases_after_exactly_66_frames_loc_bc54` (`crates/kid-core/src/tests/level_tests.rs`) drives the latch through the real contact path and pins both boundaries; `loc_bc34_damage_flash_thread_invulnerability_is_66_frames` pins the literal `66`.

### #139

- [Verify] Validated 2026-05-18 from deterministic visual bundle `.cache/recordings/issue-139-rubber-block-window/`: `cargo run -p kidcli -- verify-recording --slug issue-139-rubber-block-window --native-only` passes, and inspected frame `verify/native/000699_walk_end.png` shows the Level 00 column-80 rubber cells as round rubber-block art, not spike art. ASM cross-reference: `sub_30194` (`kid.asm:33745-33893`) sets `move.w #$FF,d4` (`kid.asm:33752`) before calling `sub_302F6` / `sub_3034A`, so the Block_Mappings lookup in `loc_30336` / `loc_3037C` masks the cell with `$00FF` and shifts left 3 — the byte offset into Block_Mappings is `(cell & 0xFF) × 8`, i.e. **the skin byte alone, not the block-type byte**. The block-type byte (cell bits 11..8) only encodes behaviour: `loc_1233C` writes type-6 rubber cells as `$E60C` (default) / `$E60E` (alternate via `loc_12372` / `loc_12380` with terrain byte at `(a3)`), and `unk_14576` keys `sub_144DA` ("Make indoor rubber block art and write it to tile $2F3-$2FA") off `Foreground_theme`. `unk_7B8DC` (`tools/to_split.txt:703` extracts $7B8DC..$7BB64 = $288 bytes verbatim into `theme/block_mappings.bin`) is loaded by `loc_11D46` as 162 longwords = 81 contiguous 8-byte quads, and `Block_Mappings` lives at `$FFFF503A..$FFFF52C2` (`variables.asm:9`); each quad holds top-left/top-right/bottom-left/bottom-right tile attribute words. Native fix: `crates/kid-render/src/level.rs` `BlockVisualMapping::resolve` uses `usize::from(skin)` for all block types, matching the documented ROM contract; `BlockVisualKind` remains diagnostic metadata only. Original concrete divergence for cell `$E60C` (rubber, skin `0x0C`): ROM byte offset `0x0C × 8 = 0x60` → tiles `$026E $0270 $026F $0271`, old native byte offset `(1 + 4×16 + 12) × 8 = 0x268` → tiles `$0AB9 $0AB7 $0ABA $0AB8` (tile $0x2B9 with hflip — completely outside the rubber-tile range $2F3..$2FA written by `sub_144DA` for indoor cell `$E60E`). Verified against the production extract at `.cache/generated/<rom-sha1>/theme/block_mappings.bin` (648 bytes = 81 × 8). Level 00 is a valid rubber-block target: generated layout `00.bin` contains `E60C` cells at columns 80 and 97. Patch lineage: commit `f75b09f8` (`render: index block mappings by skin byte`) replaced the old grouped fixture with contiguous skin-indexed quads and keeps non-standard block types on the same flat lookup path via diagnostic `BlockVisualKind::GenericBlock`. Oracle-parity result: `cargo run -p kidcli -- compare-native-oracle --scenario boot-title-start-level1` passes, so the old `level_entry@520` blocker is stale and unrelated.

### #140

- [Verify] Validated 2026-05-18 from deterministic visual bundle `.cache/recordings/issue-140-prize-block-window/`: `cargo run -p kidcli -- verify-recording --slug issue-140-prize-block-window --native-only` passes, `000150_post_first_jump.png` shows visible prize blocks using `P` art, `000239_pre_second_jump.png` shows the hit/deleted block state as block art rather than the old wrong mapping, and `000359_scenario_end.png` shows the spawned prize as a separate item sprite. Root cause was the **same pre-f75b09f8 `BlockVisualMapping::resolve` divergence as #139**: the renderer treated `theme/block_mappings.bin` as `1 fallback + 5 groups x 16 skins`, but ASM `sub_30194` (`kid.asm:33745-33893`) sets `move.w #$FF,d4` on `kid.asm:33752` so `loc_30336` / `loc_3037C` byte-index Block_Mappings as `(cell & 0xFF) × 8` — **the skin byte alone, not per-block-type**. ASM cross-reference for the prize-block lifecycle: `loc_123DC` / `loc_12408` / `loc_1241C` / `loc_12454` / `loc_12468` select the visible/disguised prize cells `$E101` / `$E102`; `sub_1007A` (`kid.asm:21345-21599`) drives the bounce coroutine — `loc_100DA..loc_10120` walk the y-position wobble (-2/+2 over 31 hibernated frames; deltas already pinned in `prize_block_wobble_y_deltas_sub_1007A`, `crates/kid-core/src/blocks.rs:1286`), `stru_101B6` keys the alternating `LnkTo_unk_E0E4E`/`LnkTo_unk_E0E5E` art frames, then the spawn-flash child at `loc_102B8` (`kid.asm:21542-21558`) plays `unk_E0F2E`/`unk_E0F36`/`unk_E0F3E`/`unk_E0F46` via `stru_102DE` and `Prize_Init_Index` (`kid.asm:21560-21576`) dispatches by prize byte to `PrizeDiamond_Init`, `PrizeHelmet*_Init`, etc.; the already-collected branch `loc_101D8` / `loc_10200` (`kid.asm:21459-21527`) replays `stru_10296` and writes `$E102` via `sub_11530`. Native cross-reference: `crates/kid-data/src/lib.rs:3105-3153` (`mapped_word_pair_sub_302F6`, `mapped_longword_sub_3034A`) implements the ROM contract: `tile_index = cell & 0x00FF`, `base = tile_index × 4` (u16 words), and `cell & 0x8000` selects between `theme_mappings` and `block_mappings`, so `$E1XX` and `$E001` cells all index Block_Mappings by skin. Native fix: `crates/kid-render/src/level.rs` `BlockVisualMapping::resolve` indexes `block_quads` by `usize::from(skin)` for every block type; `block_visual_kind` no longer changes the tile quad. Original concrete divergence for cell `$E101` (visible prize, skin `0x01`): ROM byte offset `0x01 × 8 = 0x08` → quad index 1 of Block_Mappings, old native byte offset `(1 + 1 × 16 + 1) × 8 = 0x90` → quad index 18. The disguised cell `$E102` (skin `0x02`) reads ROM offset `0x10` → quad 2 vs old native `(1 + 1 × 16 + 2) × 8 = 0x98` → quad 19. The deleted-block cell `$E001` written by `loc_101D8` via `sub_11530` reads ROM offset `0x08` → quad 1 vs old native `(1 + 0 × 16 + 1) × 8 = 0x10` → quad 2. The `theme/block_mappings.bin` extract is 648 bytes = 81 contiguous 8-byte quads; after `f75b09f8`, the renderer treats that as a flat skin-indexed table. The lifecycle wobble/spawn-flash timing itself is already pinned by `crates/kid-core/src/blocks.rs:1286` and the `prize_block_lifecycle_*` tests in `crates/kid-core/src/tests/level_tests.rs:13424-13638`; the fixed divergence was the per-frame block art, not the y-position curve. Oracle-parity result: `cargo run -p kidcli -- compare-native-oracle --scenario boot-title-start-level1` passes, so the old `level_entry@520` blocker is stale and unrelated.

- [Summary] FIXED 2026-06-06: the full-tank turret (base 0x020) now bottom-anchors on the same ground line as the treads instead of floating a frame above (native double-counted the ROM top-anchor `subi #8` via its bottom-anchor render). Structure is ASM-faithful (`Enemy0A_RockTank_Init` Tank.asm:4,68-84: body `stru_3B270` + turret `stru_3B27E` at body_y−8; native parent=body, child_attachment_snapshot=turret, sprites.rs:1277/1304/1421). So the green is a forest palette-borrow/tile-region interaction SPECIFIC to the turret tile range at 0x020: those tiles render with green (forest-borrowed palette slots 9-15, `forest_enemy_palette_with_borrowed_slots` bundle.rs) where the oracle turret is grey. So the green is NOT a palette/tile-colour bug. NOT palette/tile-colour. Verification rechecked 2026-06-06: `cargo test -q -p kidcli rock_tank_renderer_emits_body_and_turret_sprites_per_stru_3b27e -- --nocapture`. #244 folded in (duplicate). ### #152

- [Summary] Red Stealth (samurai) cannot walk up diagonal slopes that the bare Kid can
- [Verify] NOT A PORT BUG — preserved ROM quirk. ASM `loc_77C2` / `loc_77FC` (kid.asm:7857-7893) gates the standing→walking transition by helmet bitmask `%1011000101` (bits 0/2/6/7/9 = TheKid/Cyclone/IronKnight/Berzerker/Micromax). Forms outside the bitmask (Skycutter/RedStealth/Eyeclops/Juggernaut/Maniaxe) run an extra `sub_B55C` ledge probe at `(1,-1)` / `(-1,-1)`: when the diagonally-adjacent cell is `$4000` SlopeUp or `$5000` SlopeDown, the ROM stores the facing direction and branches to `loc_7828` to stay standing. TheKid is in the bitmask so it skips the probe and enters walking immediately. Native `should_hold_standing_still` (`crates/kid-core/src/movement.rs:3833`) mirrors this exactly with the same form list and the same `probe_relative_collision_sub_B55C(grid, x_px, y_px, ±1, -1)` check. The observed behaviour the user reported — "Red Stealth stops at a slope where Kid walks" — IS the original game. Workaround for players: jump over the leading slope edge; once airborne or already moving, the slope-walk path (`update_level_one_slope_ground_velocity` loc_9E6C branch for Red Stealth/Eyeclops/Maniaxe at `crates/kid-core/src/movement.rs:5907`) correctly drives ±$1000 velocity. Methodology rule: "bugs are features" — preserve.

### #154

- [Summary] Bouncy blocks invisible at the bottom of the Level 2 drop pit
- [Verify] User playtest 2026-05-19: in the section where you jump down a long hole, the rubber/bouncy blocks at the bottom physically bounce Kid back up but render as nothing visible. Engine collision works; the renderer drops the tiles. ROOT CAUSE (2026-05-19 investigation): Level 1 (Blue Lake Woods 2) has two rubber-block cells at grid (21,36)/(22,36) with skin 0x0E. `theme/block_mappings.bin` entry for skin 0x0E references VRAM tile indices 0x2F3, 0x2F5, 0x2F4, 0x2F6 — but the static `ingame/artcomp/Blocks.bin` only decompresses to 211 tiles, covering VRAM 0x0220..0x02F2 (inclusive). Tiles 0x2F3-0x2FA are **procedurally generated at level-load time** by ASM `sub_144DA` (kid.asm:27355-27420; comment in ROM: "Make indoor rubber block art and write it to tile $2F3-$2FA"): it reads four theme-specific tile descriptors via `unk_14576[Foreground_theme] * 8`, decompresses them into `Decompression_Buffer`, composites them with eight base block tiles starting at $26E using a per-nibble selection loop (`loc_1453E`), and DMAs 64 longwords to VRAM at `$5E60` (= tile $2F3). Native `resolve_ingame_vram_tile` (`crates/kidcli/src/native_player/scene.rs:731`) checks foreground (0x00BC..0x021F = 355 tiles for forest) and block (0x0220..0x02F2 = 211 tiles) ranges; tiles 0x2F3-0x2F6 fall just past the block-tile range AND outside the foreground range (which ends at 0x021F for the forest theme), so `push_tile_quad` silently drops them. Landed fix: `kid-render` now ports the `sub_144DA` generation path by using `unk_14576[theme]` to select the four terrain-mapping foreground tiles, duplicating that four-tile buffer across the eight generated tiles, and applying the `loc_1453E` nibble priority rule before appending `$2F3..$2FA` to `block_tiles`. Test data: real Level 1 layout puts these cells at (21,36)/(22,36) px (336,576); forest theme `unk_14576` entry `0xC5` resolves to foreground tiles `$1F4/$1F5/$209/$20A`. Verification: `cargo test -p kid-render`, `cargo run -p kidcli -- inspect-level --level 01`, `cargo run -p kidcli -- capture-frames --level 01 --frames 30 --layer block_overrides --output .cache/debug/issue-154-after`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `mise run verify-slice-fast` all pass.
