### #160

- [Verify] User playtest 2026-05-25 reports the game is basically silent. Root causes found: `play-native` loaded GEMS from `manifest.source_root/sound` instead of generated `manifest.output_root/sound`; native BGM theme order did not match ASM `Load_InGame loc_12004` / `unk_1201E`; and standalone GEMS queued init pointers high-to-low even though ASM `sub_E14AC` writes low-to-high. After the pointer-order fix, live `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy cargo run -q -p kidcli -- play-native --warp-level 00 --settled --record issue-160-audio-gems-pointer-order --record-frames 180` produces dynamic audio: `audio.wav` SHA-1 changed from `b822b5ce6e914a38d203dfb595a81b8057cd4603` to `fc0a5a495060c2644bc44a237a6c99277047adda`, RMS rose from `0.001119` to `0.042016`, zero crossings rose from `1` to `1570`, and `verify-recording --slug issue-160-audio-gems-pointer-order --native-only` passes. Follow-up playtest on latest-after-`3d3ee1d2` said level-start sound improved, but menu had no sound and audio basically stopped after enemy damage. Follow-up fix: native title/options shell now queues ASM `Load_TitleScreen` `bgm_Ice`, and standalone GEMS now mirrors/ages YM2612 status reads like `MdRuntime::Z80Bus`; a real-GEMS probe changed from one burst then silence to sustained non-zero RMS through `sfx_Voice_ouch`. New playtest feedback on latest audio commit: title/menu music carried into gameplay and SFX were mostly inaudible. Root cause: native queued GEMS stop-all as `FF 16`, but the driver command reads a sequence id byte and uses `$FF` to mean all sequences; the next `PlaySound` marker was swallowed as that argument and the level BGM start bytes were ignored. Native now queues `FF 16 FF` before starting the new BGM sequence, with a regression locking the following `FF 10 <bgm>` command intact. 2026-05-25 rejected hypothesis: moving standalone command FIFO from `$1A40` to reference GEMS 2.8 `$1B40` silenced later queued SFX entirely in `.cache/recordings/issue-160-audio-after-damage-cmdfifo`, so Kid's extracted driver layout still expects `$1A40`. Previous fix: direct settled native gameplay no longer queues stop-all before the first level BGM, and cue replacements defer the new start by one audio frame after stop-all. Evidence: `.cache/recordings/issue-160-audio-current-settled-after-startonly` raises global RMS from `0.017301` to `0.049685`, has `80/80` non-zero 0.1s windows instead of `22/80`, and `verify-recording --slug issue-160-audio-current-settled-after-startonly --native-only` passes. Latest playtest still heard title music under gameplay with weak SFX; ASM check shows Kid's `StopMusic` at `kid.asm:49727` reloads/resets the GEMS driver and queues `$0B` pointer init, not `$16` stop-all. Native music replacement now calls `GemsAudioEngine::stop_music()` before deferring the next BGM start; `cargo run -q -p kidcli -- verify-audio-output --scenario boot-title-start-level1` passes. Latest native listening bundle: `.cache/recordings/issue-160-audio-latest-validation/audio.wav` from `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy cargo run -q -p kidcli -- play-native --warp-level 00 --settled --record issue-160-audio-latest-validation --record-frames 600` verifies native-only, is 10.00s stereo at 44.1 kHz, and has RMS `0.052095`, peak `0.367125`, and `100/100` 0.1s windows above 0.001 RMS. New playtest feedback: title music still carried into gameplay and SFX were mostly absent; native `play-native` was clearing the active title BGM cue during the intervening `LevelTransition` shell, so the first `InGame` frame started level music without the ASM `StopMusic` reset. The BGM state helper now preserves the previous cue through non-BGM shell frames and only switches on the next concrete cue, forcing title-to-level replacement through `StopMusicThenStart`. Validated 2026-05-25: `mise run human-validation-review` passes the `issue-160-audio-latest-validation` recording, `cargo run -q -p kidcli -- verify-audio-output --scenario boot-title-start-level1` passes, and the native audio trace for `boot_title_start_level1` shows GEMS resets plus fresh YM2612 key-ons after the title-to-gameplay transition. Follow-up 2026-05-26: refreshed settled enemy-contact recording `.cache/recordings/issue-160-audio-current-enemy-contact` reaches damage at frames 290 and 356, then death/restart at 431; `verify-recording --slug issue-160-audio-current-enemy-contact --native-only` passes, and the 10.00s stereo `audio.wav` has all `100/100` 0.1s windows above 0.001 RMS through and after both damage events. The old silent `issue-138-enemy-contact/audio.wav` is stale pre-fix evidence. Current status 2026-06-02: blocked on a concrete human/real-device repro. Current main has audible rendered and live-SDL waveform evidence for cold intro and deterministic title/options routes, with no SDL queue starvation or queue errors.

### #169

- [Verify] Fixed 2026-05-25: first concrete mismatch was rendering, not the whole Drips state machine. Native was drawing `DripsSurfaceCrawler` with the falling-child `LnkTo_unk_C7B26` frame even though ASM `Drips.asm off_33520` uses `LnkTo_unk_C7B9E`/`LnkTo_unk_C7BA6` for the surface/crawler frames. Follow-up placement root cause: native ceiling attach used a 1px probe, but ASM `object_meta=$16` maps through `CollisionSize_Index` to `unk_314D0` (`top=-$1F,height=$1F`) and `GfxObjects_Collision loc_1A6C` snaps from that hitbox. Latest playtest says the slime should drip from beta blocks until a large enough pool gathers, but native has slime floating and then dripping in Level 2. Follow-up 2026-05-25 hides the parent/controller enemy sprite in the native player because ASM `Enemy16_Drip_Init` / `loc_33488` keeps that gfx object hidden via `$13`; visible falling and crawler children remain rendered through typed projectile snapshots. Follow-up 2026-05-25 wires the `off_33520` pool cursor so the first two falling-child splashes are pool-growth entries and only the negative sentinel path may allocate `loc_335D8`, matching the "drip until pool gathers" cadence. Final fix holds the parent/controller at `DRIPS_DROP_IN_FLIGHT_TIMER` after `loc_33424` and advances/reseeds the pool only when the child hits terrain at `loc_33488`; this prevents stacked/floating slime while a falling child is still active. Regression: `drips_owned_drop_advances_pool_and_reseeds_parent_only_on_splash_loc_33488`; verification: `cargo test -p kid-core drips -- --nocapture`.

### #204

- [Summary] REOPENED 2026-06-03 (Samurai/Red Stealth still cannot slide down). Non-walking forms (Red Stealth/Eyeclops/Maniaxe/Skycutter/Juggernaut) jitter on a slope instead of sliding down
- [Verify] FIXED + ORACLE-VERIFIED 2026-06-04. The 2026-06-04 deferred ASM-only hypothesis ("Red Stealth should NOT slide on current-row, flip the slide tests") was WRONG — the oracle disproves it. Built the clean probe the prior session couldn't: `.cache/debug/issue-204-redstealth-downhill.json` (warp L0, `settle_oracle_warp`, `playtest_form:3`, `start_position` on the col-113 SlopeDown plateau, hold Right). `tas-diff` vs jgenesis is FRAME-IDENTICAL through frame 38; at frame 39 the oracle enters `character_movement=6` (slope-walk) and descends ~3px/frame BOTH axes (x 1813→2025, y 197→335), while pre-fix native stayed `character_movement=2` pinned at x≈1808/y≈193 (the #204 jitter). So Red Stealth DOES slide down a current-row SlopeDown; the bug was native re-running the `loc_8E98` current-row tile-snap every frame (the per-frame `step_with_order_inner` AsmFaithful dispatch, movement.rs:3079 guard) and yanking the slide back whenever `y_pos` oscillated into the slope's own row → limit cycle. ROOT CAUSE: ASM reaches `loc_8E98` only from the MoveID 2 walking dispatch (`loc_8E3E`); once `loc_9D22` sets MoveID 6 the slope-walk loop (`loc_9D58`/`loc_9E6C`) owns dispatch and NEVER re-runs `loc_8E3E`. Native had no persistent MoveID-6 state so it re-evaluated the tile-snap each frame. FIX: added `TerrainState.slope_sliding` (types.rs) mirroring MoveID 6 — set when `update_horizontal_velocity_only` drives slope velocity on a current-row slope, cleared on leaving the slope to flat/solid or when `should_hold_standing_still` returns to standing; gated the movement.rs:3079 `loc_8E98` tile-snap with `!self.terrain.slope_sliding`. Engine-level, no per-level hacks. After fix the oracle probe is 22/24 MATCH over the descent (2 residual = single-frame `kid_y_vel` blips at tile-boundary re-snaps + slope-exit timing, position always matched). The pre-existing slide tests (`asm_faithful_red_stealth_on_current_slope_up_enters_loc_9e6c_slide` etc.) were NOT flipped — the oracle confirms they assert the correct behaviour. New regression: `asm_faithful_red_stealth_current_slopedown_slide_latch_gates_loc_8e98_tilesnap_issue_204` (movement_tests.rs; uses `PhysicsOrder::AsmFaithful` because the guard lives only in that path; verified to FAIL with the gate disabled). #152 standing-at-up-slope-edge tests stay green. Gate: kid-core lib 5542 pass / 0 fail, kidcli gameplay_regression 8/8, clippy -D warnings clean, typos clean. PRIOR-FIX HISTORY (2026-05-29 `ebf2704c`/`f4df2184`): #152's adjacent-slope walk-UP hold remains faithful, but current slope support now bypasses `should_hold_standing_still` so `loc_7820`/`loc_8D72` can reach `sub_9386` and `loc_9E6C` downhill slide. Regressions: `asm_faithful_red_stealth_on_current_slope_up_enters_loc_9e6c_slide`, `asm_faithful_red_stealth_current_slope_up_slides_without_limit_cycle`, `asm_faithful_eyeclops_on_current_slope_down_enters_loc_9e6c_slide`, `asm_faithful_eyeclops_current_slope_down_slides_without_limit_cycle`, with adjacent-hold coverage still pinned by `asm_faithful_loc_77c2_non_bitmask_slope_up_holds_standing_right` and `asm_faithful_loc_77fc_non_bitmask_slope_down_holds_standing_left`. Gate: `mise run verify-slice-fast` passed in the fixing session; focused tests re-run 2026-05-29. ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-06-04 (ASM-cited; fix NOT applied — needs a clean slope oracle probe to verify, deferred per never-guess-on-movement): the 2026-05-29 fix's PREMISE is wrong. ASM dispatch loc_8E80 (kid.asm:10249) / loc_8E98 (kid.asm:10259), keyed on `sub_9386` (kid.asm:10809) d7 = CURRENT-row slope (own cell $4000/$5000) → d7=−1 vs NEXT-row slope (one row below) → d7=+1: for d7=+1 (next-row), Red Stealth/Eyeclops/Maniaxe → loc_9D22 → loc_9E6C SLIDE; for d7=−1 (current-row), the `$2C5` bitmask {TheKid,Cyclone,IronKnight,Berzerker,Micromax} slides but **Red Stealth is NOT in it** → it edge-snaps `(x&$FFF0)−1` (loc_8E98), does NOT slide. The slide arithmetic loc_9E6C (movement.rs:6513) is correct. So Red Stealth should slide only when the slope is the NEXT row below its feet (i.e. while descending), not on the current-row tile. The 2026-05-29 guard (movement.rs:4087-4100, forcing should_hold_standing_still=false on any current-row slope cell) makes current-row slopes wrongly feed loc_9E6C → the limit-cycle (slide 1 frame, snap back) = the observed jitter/no-slide. Its regression tests (`asm_faithful_red_stealth_on_current_slope_up_enters_loc_9e6c_slide` etc., movement_tests.rs:15876+) encode the WRONG assumption. Oracle probe (Red Stealth helmet 3 on a slope, tas-diff vs jgenesis): oracle slides ~960px downhill then rests; native pins with ±0x1d400 jitter, zero net = #204. FIX (next session, with a clean grounded-on-slope probe): make the dispatch distinguish d7=−1 current-row (edge-snap for non-$2C5 forms) from d7=+1 next-row (slide), and correct the wrong-assumption tests. Couldn't build a frame-0-identical probe this pass: placement floor-snap/form-width settle moves native off the level-0 SlopeUp foot (also the #152 confound), and Level 2 slopes aren't reachable by scripted walking — a synthetic SlopeDown grid through the oracle, or a real-input Level-2 capture, is needed.

### #216

- [Verify] Evidence source: human playtest after pushed commits. Symptoms: block break and diamond collection sounds are delayed; level-complete sound does not finish cleanly. #160 covers continuous BGM/SFX output but not these event-specific timing edges. 2026-06-04 ASM trace investigation found two concrete, state-verifiable timing bugs and fixed them. (1) Diamond delay: ASM `PrizeDiamondCollected_Init` (kid.asm:21101-21162) plays `sfx_Diamond_prize` ($2D) on the *contact* frame at loc_2510C, then runs a 32-frame fly-to-counter loop before `Number_Diamonds` increments. Native fired the cue from the `diamond_count > prev` heuristic, i.e. ~33 frames late (the `PRIZE_DIAMOND_AWARD_DELAY_FRAMES` window). Fix: `queue_prize_diamond_award` now pushes `QueuedSoundEffect::DiamondPrize` into the core trace at contact; the native-player count-increase heuristic was removed. (2) Level-complete cut-off: ASM plays `sfx_Score_counter` ($0C) *twice* — at drain start (loc_D770, kid.asm:16850-16852) and again at drain end via `j_PlaySound2` (loc_D7F4, kid.asm:16906-16908). Native emitted only the drain-start cue, so the EOL jingle ended abruptly. Fix: new trace field `level_complete_score_counter_drained` (derived from `eol_score_counter_duration_loc_D770().counter_frames`) drives a second SCORE_COUNTER cue on the drain-complete rising edge. REAL-DEVICE-BLOCKED remainder: "block break sound delayed" was NOT reproduced as a state-level timing bug — block-hit/destroy cues already fire on the contact frame (`blocks_hit_this_frame` / `block_destroy_effects`), and metal/rubber/prize block ids are ASM-correct ($12/$56/$11). Any residual block-break or level-complete *playback-quality* lag (envelope/release length, GEMS mixing) is heuristic-sequencer fidelity, not event timing, and needs human/real-device listening — it cannot be verified from the trace. Audio synthesis quality more broadly is the heuristic-vs-full-GEMS-sequencer scope tracked under #160. STATUS 2026-06-04: the two state-verifiable timing fixes are complete and gate-verified (3 cited regressions re-run green); moved [~] to [?] — remainder is real-device listening, folded into #160.

- CORRECTION 2026-06-19 (loc_D7F4 semantics): the 2026-06-04 note above mislabelled the drain-end cue as a "second *play* of sfx_Score_counter". Direct reading of the GEMS driver source (`.cache/references/gemsplay/GemsPlay_2-0.c` case 18) establishes GEMS `$10` = `cmdstartseq` (start sequence N) and `$12` = `cmdstopseq` (**stop** sequence N, matches `CCBSNUM`); `$16` = `cmdstopall`. So loc_D752 *starts* the score-counter tick via `j_PlaySound` (`$10`) and loc_D7F4 *stops* it via `j_PlaySound2` (`$12`) at drain-complete — cleanly silencing the tick once the tally lands, which is exactly the #216 "does not finish cleanly" want. The native `kid-md::GemsAudioEngine` runs the real Z80 driver binary, so it already honoured `$12` = stop; rendered audio was faithful — the defect was purely backwards Rust naming/docs. Renamed the command model to `StartSequence`/`StopSequence` (see the GEMS-rename commits) and relabelled this drain-end cue + its tests (`play_native_stops_eol_score_counter_at_loc_d7f4`, `scripted_recording_audio_events_label_loc_d7f4_score_counter_as_stopsequence`). Command-level corroboration: a fresh `record-scenario-file` of the EOL route emits `frame=314 command=StartSequence(12)` (drain begins) then `frame=558 command=StopSequence(12)` (drain completes) for sequence `$0C`; `audio.wav` written to `.cache/recordings/issue216-eol-stop-verify/` for human listen. Relates #265 (EOL audio), #339 (RockTank drive stop uses the same `$12` cmdstopseq), #341 (per-SFX `audio-audit` tool would give command-level oracle verification). Still `[?]` — the perceptual-listen confirmation remains a human step; do not close.

### #224

- [Summary] Compound `$14/$18` slope-corner collision response — DEFERRED: unreachable in normal play (stuck-in-solid recovery only)

ASM correction: `$14`=`colid_slopeup`, `$18`=`colid_slopedown` (constants.asm:169-170), NOT "floor+wall"; the dispatch is recovery-SNAP (non-Jugg/Sky → `loc_B9A2`/`loc_BA5A`) + diagonal BOUNCE-OUT (Jugg/Sky → `loc_A556`/`loc_A5AE`), there is NO crush-kill. `GfxObjects_Collision` only writes `$14/$18` to Kid (ChkUpSlope/ChkDownSlope, `loc_1A94`/`loc_1AB8`) when Kid's hitbox straddles a SOLID tile AND an adjacent SLOPE tile after the compound diagonal integration has embedded Kid inside the junction — i.e. stuck-in-solid recovery. Oracle (jgenesis) reproduction needed Kid's live x_pos/y_pos PATCHED into the hollow interior of a fully-enclosed solid pyramid (level 0 cells ~(48..54,11..16), col 50 row 13 walled on 4 sides): oracle then snaps Kid ~40px up onto the slope surface (y 222→182 = `loc_B9A2`; snap math `(col+row)*16+15-x_pos` = `terrain::slope_floor_y`). Approaching the SAME corners from OPEN AIR (only normal-play path): `collision_type` stays 0, oracle walks the slope, native (decomposed per-axis) tracks within 6px tolerance — no divergence. The per-axis pipeline never embeds Kid in solid, so the `$14/$18` precondition cannot arise without an artificial probe teleport. Porting the snap would add a dead stuck-in-solid branch. Finding + corrected ASM documented at `movement.rs:3300-3392`. Relates #207.

### #229

- [Summary] Level-loading fidelity: `Load_Level` tail modelled but dead; live load delegates terrain/block decode to the emulator dump
- [Verify] Advanced 2026-06-02: native `level_bounds()` now matches ASM `Load_LevelData loc_15A0` for the header height top bits by adding `Number_blank_top_rows` after the base 14-block screen-height calculation, so camera/death/enemy active bounds include the inserted top rows. Regression `load_leveldata_height_flags_extend_level_bounds_loc_15a0` failed at 448px before the patch and now expects 544px for `height_screens=2,height_flag_bits=3`. Still open: level-loading fidelity audit 2026-05-30 (`docs/source-port/audits/level-loading-fidelity-audit.md`, same workflow) found 18 units, 55 gaps (18 high, 19 medium, 18 low). Most of `Load_Level`'s tail (palette/art/background/scroll/music) is modelled helper-for-helper but dead; the live loader `reload_block_grid_for_level` (`level.rs:17537`) loads only the collision grid + block list + murder wall + weather. **Architectural:** terrain + block-layout decode are delegated to the jgenesis emulator RAM dump (`inspect.rs:1023`), not implemented natively — `Decompress_Chunk`, `AddrTbl_BlockTypes` block-type dispatch, `LoadBlockLayout`, and the theme-collision index have no live native representation (terrain is faithful only for pre-dumped levels). Genuine bug split to child #235 (non-oracle terrain fallback corruption). Evidence: ASM-vs-native, adversarially verified. Gate: per-unit regression + new load scenario + `mise run verify-slice-fast`. DECODER SPIKE 2026-06-03 (Step 0 done): `dump-level-layout` now also dumps `Level_terrain_layout` ($FF52C2) to `<id>.terrain.bin`. Comparing live terrain vs the bundle decoded `foreground.bin` for L01 (160×42) CRACKS the layout mystery that caused prior reconstruction to mismatch 81.8%: bundle `foreground.bin` = 6720 B = 160×42 ROW-MAJOR FG **tile-render** indices (0x0d,0x0e,…); live `Level_terrain_layout` = 8400 B = **30 screens × $118 (20×14 cells/screen) SCREEN-MAJOR collision-terrain bytes** — different size/stride/content, so they are NOT interchangeable. CRUCIALLY the byte VALUES also differ (terrain[0]=0x1b,0x2d,0x1d,0x2e…; fg[0]=0x0d,0x0e,0x0b,0x0c,0x11…), not just the stride — so the bundle `foreground.bin` is a RENDER-oriented tile-index layout, while `Level_terrain_layout` holds the raw FG/skin bytes that `loc_11C34` feeds through `ThemeCollision[byte]` to build `Level_Layout` (low byte = skin = the terrain byte; high nibble = collision). `Level_Layout` ($FFFFA652, $41A0 = 8400 cells × 2) working fixtures read correctly as width×height row-major. So the bundle's decoded fg is NOT the decoder input; the decoder needs the RAW FG resource decompressed into the $118 screen-major terrain byte buffer. FURTHER (Step 1 done): `<id>.terrain.bin` (1b,2d,1d,2e…) matches NONE of the bundle's decoded layers — `foreground.bin`(0d0e render tiles), `block.bin`(442 B object list), `background.bin`(50 B scroll). So `Level_terrain_layout` is GENERATED AT RUNTIME by `Load_Level` (decompress FG resource into the $118 screen-major skin buffer); it is not a reshaped/remapped bundle asset. CONCLUSION: the native decoder must port the ROM terrain generation (`Decompress_Chunk` of the FG resource into the $118=20×14-per-screen buffer) — there is no shortcut via existing bundle files. EXACT ASM (kid.asm:23792-23829): header `(a0)+` = "tile layout address"; `move.w (a0)+,d0; lea (a0,d0.w),a1` splits a control-pointer (a0) and data-pointer (a1); `loc_11C10: bsr Decompress_Chunk` loops into `Level_terrain_layout`; then `loc_11C34/11C36` writes `Level_Layout` cell = `[ThemeCollision_Index[theme][byte]<<4, byte]` per cell across width×height (NOTE: this loop is WIDTH×HEIGHT row-major, confirming Level_Layout is row-major even though the terrain buffer is allocated $118-strided). OPEN PUZZLE to resolve before the port: `decode_saxman(level/foreground/<id>.bin)` (the bundle path, no remap — lib.rs:4091) yields `0d0e…`, but the ROM's `Decompress_Chunk` of the tile-layout resource yields `1b2d…`. The recon equated Decompress_Chunk with Saxman, so either (a) Decompress_Chunk (kid.asm:26143) is NOT the same algorithm as `decode_saxman`, or (b) the bundle's `foreground` resource pointer ≠ the ROM header's tile-layout pointer. PUZZLE RESOLVED 2026-06-03: diffed `Decompress_Chunk` (kid.asm:26143-26210) vs `decode_saxman` (lib.rs:4231) — SAME algorithm (literal / `00` short-ref / `01` long-ref with `$7FF` 11-bit distance = 3 high bits + 1 data byte; same bit-state resume). So the decompressor is already ported as `decode_saxman`. Therefore the bundle's `level/foreground/<id>.bin` is NOT the tile-layout resource `loc_11BEC` decompresses (it must be a different header pointer / a render-graphics layer), since same-algorithm+same-resource would give identical bytes but they differ (0d0e vs 1b2d). DECODER PORT (now small, no new decompressor needed): (1) extract/locate the correct "tile layout" resource — the FIRST long after flag pos in the level header (formats.txt order: FG-tile-layout, block, bg, enemy) — whichever decode_saxmans to the 1b2d skin terrain; (2) `decode_saxman` it; (3) run the already-ported row-major collision map `level_layout_cells_loc_11C34` with `ThemeCollision_Index[theme]` (theme/collision/<theme>.bin) to build Level_Layout low=skin/high=collision; (4) block overlay loc_11C7E; (5) verify byte-equal to `<id>.bin` fixtures across all fixtured levels; (6) wire into `load_block_grid_for_level` for the 4 unreachable bonus levels. The header field/resource identification is the only remaining unknown. UPDATE 2026-06-03: actually the bundle DID split the FG tile-layout pointer into `level/foreground/<id>.bin` (2948 B compressed for L01), so it IS the resource `loc_11BEC` decompresses. Yet `decode_saxman(foreground/01.bin)`=0d0e while ROM `Decompress_Chunk` of the same →1b2d. Same input+same-algorithm can't differ, so the contradiction means either `decode_saxman` ≠ `Decompress_Chunk` (note: Decompress_Chunk is CHUNKED/RESUMABLE — called in a loop `loc_11C10` with d2 selecting a bit-position resume entry Decompress_BitPos0..6, and writes screen-major to the $118 buffer; `decode_saxman` is a single contiguous pass) OR `foreground.bin` is not literally `decode_saxman(foreground/01.bin)`. EXACT NEXT EXPERIMENT (Rust harness, ~20 lines): `assert decode_saxman(read("level/foreground/01.bin")) == read("decoded/level/01/foreground.bin")` (confirm the export identity), then compare that decoded output against `01.terrain.bin` (the new dump) cell-for-cell modulo the $118 screen-major stride. If they match → decoder is just decode_saxman + stride-reshape + loc_11C34 (trivial). If they differ → port Decompress_Chunk's chunked/resumable variant. This single test resolves the decoder approach. EXPERIMENT RUN 2026-06-03 (throwaway kid-data example, since removed): `decode_saxman(level/foreground/01.bin)` == `decoded/level/01/foreground.bin` EXACTLY (0d0e…, 6720 B) — confirms the export identity. And that decoded output ≠ `01.terrain.bin` (1b2d…, 8400 B). So the terrain skin layer is NOT decode_saxman of the bundle's foreground resource. foreground/01.bin (2948 B) is the only raw resource large enough to decompress to 6720 cells, yet it yields render tiles (0d0e), not skins. CONCLUSION: either the ROM builds Level_terrain_layout from a resource/pointer the bundle does not currently extract (read the full ROM level header to enumerate ALL layout pointers — header/01.bin is only 12 B, so the bundle stores a reduced header; the 4 layout longs are resolved during extraction), or Decompress_Chunk genuinely differs from decode_saxman on this resource. RESOLVED 2026-06-03: `mapheader_definitions.asm` shows L01 = `maphdr "header/01.bin", ForegroundLayout_01, BlockLayout_01.bin, BackgroundLayout_01, EnemyLayout_01`. The `header/01.bin` is 12 inline bytes (dims/theme/player+flag pos); the FIRST layout long `loc_11BEC` decompresses is `ForegroundLayout_01` = the bundle's `level/foreground/01.bin`. So the terrain SOURCE is confirmed = `foreground/01.bin` (the SAME resource the bundle saxman-decodes). Since `decode_saxman(foreground/01.bin)`=0d0e but the ROM `Decompress_Chunk` of it →1b2d terrain, and one resource has one compression, **`Decompress_Chunk` is a genuinely different algorithm from `decode_saxman`** (despite similar surface structure; note its chunked/resumable d2 bit-position entry + screen-major $118 writes). decode_saxman's 0d0e is a red herring for terrain (whatever `foreground_layout` uses it for at scene.rs:3047 is a separate concern). COMPLETE DECODER PLAN: port `Decompress_Chunk` (kid.asm:26143-26874) in Rust; run it on `foreground/<id>.bin`; assert output == `<id>.terrain.bin` (the new dump) for all fixtured levels; then row-major `loc_11C34` collision map (`level_layout_cells_loc_11C34`, ported) with `theme/collision/<theme>.bin` + block overlay `loc_11C7E` → assert byte-equal to `<id>.bin` Level_Layout fixtures; finally wire into `load_block_grid_for_level` so the 4 unreachable bonus levels (logical 5A/5D/5E/63) get correct terrain (closes #246 + the bonus half of #238). Everything except the `Decompress_Chunk` port itself is already in place + verifiable against the dumped fixtures. ★ BREAKTHROUGH 2026-06-03 (CORRECTS the above): NO Decompress_Chunk port is needed. The earlier "Decompress_Chunk ≠ decode_saxman / terrain=1b2d" finding was a LOGICAL-vs-RESOURCE ID MIXUP: `dump-level-layout --level 01` warps to LOGICAL 01 = `map_order[1]` = resource 0x4B, but `foreground/01.bin` is RESOURCE 0x01. `map_order[4]`=0x01, so dumping LOGICAL 4 gives resource-0x01 terrain. VERIFIED: `decode_saxman(foreground/01.bin)` (6720 B) == `dump-level-layout --level 04 → 04.terrain.bin[0..6720]` BYTE-IDENTICAL (`0d0e 0b0c 1112 1314 cf34 0095 9697 9895…`; terrain tail is zero-pad to $20D0). So `Level_terrain_layout = decode_saxman(FG resource)` packed row-major (the $118 "screens" is just the buffer allocation; real data is width×height then zero-padded). FINAL DECODER (wiring, not porting): for a logical level, `r = resource_level_id(level)`; `terrain = decode_saxman(read(foreground/<r>.bin))`; theme from header; `Level_Layout cell = [ThemeCollision[theme][terrain_byte]<<4, terrain_byte]` via the ported `level_layout_cells_loc_11C34` (theme/collision/<theme>.bin); then block overlay `loc_11C7E` from BlockLayout_<r>. Verify byte-equal to `<logical>.bin` fixtures, then wire `load_block_grid_for_level` for the 4 bonus levels. decode_saxman + collision map are BOTH already implemented — the port is small. ★ LANDED 2026-06-03: `decode_level_layout` (level.rs:17753) implements decode_saxman(foreground)→`level_layout_cells_loc_11C34` collision map→BlockGrid, wired as the fixture-absent fallback in `load_block_grid_for_level`. Tests `decode_level_layout_matches_fixture_collision_cells_loc_11c34` (byte-equal plain collision cells, 84/96 levels, 396,871 cells; 12 skipped = the #235 skin/dim-aliased set), `decode_level_layout_gives_unreachable_bonus_levels_a_floor`, `load_block_grid_for_level_falls_back_to_native_decoder` — all pass; gate green (5538+8), clippy clean. REMAINING for full #229 closure: port the block-overlay pass `loc_11C7E` + `sub_127A8` (the `$E0xx` base cells + `$20`/flag overlays) so decoder-only levels also get block-placed collision (currently TODO(fidelity); floors/walls are exact so falling-deaths are fixed). ★ DECOMPRESSOR LANDED 2026-06-03 (CORRECTS earlier "absent from disassembly" claims): `LoadBlockLayout` is NOT absent — it IS at kid.asm:25557 (`loc_132A6`), bit-reader helpers `sub_13618`/`sub_13622`/`sub_1363C`/`sub_1364C`/`loc_13650` at kid.asm:26062-26121 (prior grep missed them because kid.asm has embedded binary — use `rg -a`/`sed`). The "block resource is NOT the same Saxman format" note is correct, but the conclusion "decompressor body absent / cannot port without guessing" was wrong: LoadBlockLayout is a DISTINCT format that REUSES the EniDec MSB-first bit reader (already ported as `EnigmaBitReader`). Ported as `kid_data::decode_block_layout` (lib.rs, after decode_enigma): header = 8 discarded bits + 4-bit X-width (sentinel `(1<<X)-1`) + 4-bit Y-width; main loop `loc_132D6` reads 1 flag bit (ror→bit15) + 5-bit type (`$1F`=terminator), dispatches via `off_132FC` to 11 per-type entry decoders (loc_1331E/1334C/133A0/133DE/1342E/1345E/1347C). Resources need 8 trailing zero pad bytes (ROM reader pre-fetches past the sliced resource end — same margin decode_enigma uses). VERIFIED: all 103 block resources decode to clean `$FFFF`-terminated streams; cross-validating each stream through a throwaway `loc_11C7E` overlay vs the live `Level_Layout` fixtures collapsed the per-level diff from the 6.4% no-overlay baseline to only the cells of the few still-unported overlay handlers — proving the decompressor OUTPUT is correct, not merely well-formed. Tests: `block_layout_05_decodes_to_expected_word_stream_loc_132a6` (golden stream for smallest real resource, kid-data) + `loc_132a6_decodes_block_layout_words_into_the_ffff_terminated_stream` (kid-core wrapper; the old wrongly-Enigma test was replaced). The kid-core wrapper `decode_block_layout_loc_132A6` now delegates to the real decoder (was wrongly calling `decode_enigma`). NOT yet wired into `decode_level_layout`'s live path: the integrated `loc_11C7E`/`AddrTbl_BlockTypes` overlay DRIVER is still missing (existing helpers are isolated unit fns), and several handlers (loc_124A6 type3, loc_1253A shooter, loc_126F2 type16 corner-bset) need their cell-write paths assembled to byte-equality first; left out to keep the gate green. ★ OVERLAY DRIVER LANDED 2026-06-03 (full chain byte-equal): `apply_block_overlay_loc_11C7E` (level.rs) ports the integrated `loc_11C7E` + `AddrTbl_BlockTypes` (17-entry longword table) dispatch and ALL handlers — loc_122B8 base-cell (types 0/2/5/7/9 → word_122C6 `$E001/$E203/$E50B/$E710/$E919`), loc_123DC type1 prize (`$E101/$E102` from per-cell property word), loc_124A6 type3 ghost (`$E304` fill gated on the 8-word record's `$A(a1)` field), loc_1263C type4 (`$E407/$E408` pair), loc_1233C type6 (terrain-dependent `$E60C/$E60E`), loc_1253A type8 shooter (2×2 `$B811..$B814`), loc_125A6 types10/12 (`(d5&$FF)−$15E4`/`−$13D3`), loc_126BA type11 (`$EB2C`), loc_126F2 type16 corner (byte_1274E class nibble + sub_12752 neighbour bset), and the `tst.w d0; bmi` hidden-block path (sub_127A8 `$20` / skin) on every handler. WARP-CAMERA ROOT CAUSE NARROWED 2026-06-04 (high-leverage: this mismatch blocks oracle reproduction for the whole #249/#250/#213/#214/#252 playtest set): native=`0x0280` (640px) IS the ASM-correct bootstrap — `initialise_camera_bootstrap_loc_11F48` (level.rs:9008, kid.asm:24129) floors player_start_x to a 320px (`$140`) screen, and native matches that. So the blocker is a SETTLE-DYNAMICS difference (post-bootstrap camera-follow during the warp-settle frames), NOT a bootstrap-formula error — native's settle leaves the camera screen-floored while the oracle's warp lets it track Kid. FIX DIRECTION: match the oracle's per-frame camera-follow through the warp-settle window (compare camera_x frame-by-frame from the bootstrap to frame 0) so the settled warp lands on the oracle's tracked camera, not the floored bootstrap. Resolving this is the unlock for the entire oracle-reproduction phase. The idle sweep masks camera only because those warped checkpoints are oracle-unreliable; it is NOT a blanket-advisory field. So making `verify-tas` ignore camera at frame 0 would HIDE real divergences when the oracle is reliable — wrong fix. The genuine fix is engine-side: match the oracle's warp-settle camera-follow so native lands on the oracle's tracked camera (744) rather than the floored bootstrap (640). This is deep settle-dynamics work (a focused pass), confirmed not collapsible to a verifier tweak. TRACED TO THE SETTLE LOOP 2026-06-04: `level_respawn_slice_with_floor_snap_inner` (level.rs:18604) DOES run the camera-follow — it steps up to 180 settle frames via `slice.step` (full physics incl. camera) until 8 stable frames, then `finish_respawn_camera_convergence` (only converges Y, a +2px grounded beat). So native 640 vs oracle 744 is EITHER the convergence stopping short of centre OR native's Kid spawn-x sitting ~104px left of the oracle's (camera centres on Kid in both). DISTINGUISHING STEP (the exact next action): capture the ORACLE's per-frame warp-settle trace directly (run the emulator alone through the warp, record `camera_x_pos` and `kid_x_pos` each settle frame) and diff against native's `RespawnSettleFrame` trace (the inner already records one via `settle_trace`) — if oracle kid_x matches native but camera diverges, fix the convergence endpoint; if kid_x diverges, it is a spawn-x bug. ### #245

- [Summary] 2026-06-03 playtest: dying can leave the screen black/frozen (looks stuck)
- [Verify] FIXED 2026-06-04: root cause was a one-frame-late death-arc launch introduced by commit `0108599e` (Defer player contact damage to next object pass). That commit deferred ALL player contact damage by one frame to fix the #211 walk route, but the death-causing landing-dragon graze already had a one-frame landing-defer guard (`2572ebf2`), so the deferral double-delayed it: death landed on frame 1685 instead of the oracle's 1684, shifting the entire death→tumble→lose_life→respawn sequence one frame. Follow-up commit `40b205e9` then bumped `PLAYER_DEATH_HIDE_FRAMES` 32→40 (+SHELL/CAMERA) to compensate, over-shifting the hidden window by ~8 frames and drifting the visible respawn bootstrap from oracle frame 1791 to ~1799. The death-respawn cache-backed regression tests were left red on main with values matching neither native nor oracle. Fix: apply the grounded dragon-graze contact in-frame (combat.rs ~10558) instead of queueing it, so the death lands on oracle frame 1684; restore `PLAYER_DEATH_HIDE_FRAMES=32` (keeping the loc_b8de Level-2 `HIDE-SHELL`/`HIDE-CAMERA` relationships). Verified against oracle window `death_respawn_level1_window_01700_01855_step_1`: tumble arc, lose_life (f1759), bootstrap pose (f1791 `(0x160,0x44)`), and slide-to-hold (f1855 `(0x40,0x68)`) all byte-match. All 7 previously-failing `death_respawn_level_1_*` cache-backed tests now pass (cache-backed kid-core failures 73→66, the remaining 66 are unrelated published_tas/demo/snapshot/IntroSequence/prize-cell). Known residual: the invisible hidden-pose/camera `None`-clear is one frame early on Level 1 because the hide window is a single global constant that Level 1 (`HIDE-SHELL=11`) and the Level 2 loc_b8de probe (`HIDE-SHELL=13`) genuinely disagree on — a per-route oracle-derived hide window is the proper follow-up (does not affect the visible respawn). Min gate: 1p-playable. REJECTED-APPROACH 2026-06-04: an oracle probe found a SEPARATE minor residual — on a STEADY walk into the Level-0 walking dragon (kid_y_velocity==0 throughout, no landing frame) native applies the contact graze ONE FRAME EARLY (number_hitpoints drops at frame 60 vs oracle frame 61). Cause: the grounded DragonWalking graze consumes in-frame (correct for THIS #245 landing case, where the falling frame absorbs the defer), but a steady-grounded walk-in has no landing frame so it should defer one frame via the shared pending_player_contact_damage queue. Routing the grounded graze UNIFORMLY through the pending queue FIXES the steady-walk case but REGRESSES #245 (verified: 7 death_respawn_level_1_* tests fail — re-introduces the double-delay, death at 1685 not 1684). So the correct fix must DISTINGUISH landing (airborne->ground this frame -> in-frame consume) from steady-grounded (defer); a uniform approach cannot satisfy both. Deferred — minor 1-frame damage-timing on the L0 dragon steady-walk only; #245's visible death-respawn is correct.

### #247

- [Summary] Theme collision table trimmed: high skin indices lose their real ROM collision nibble (was misattributed to the closed #235)
- [Verify] FIXED 2026-06-03: the bundle slices each `theme/collision/<name>.bin` at the NEXT pointer (`.cache/upstream/kid-chameleon-disasm/tools/to_split.txt:15-25`), so e.g. `swamp.bin` is 252 B (own length). But ASM loc_11C36 (`kid.asm:23818`) indexes `ThemeCollision_Index[theme]` with the FULL 8-bit skin byte (`move.b (a0,d2.w),d3`) and the tables are packed contiguously (`unk_7BB64`..`unk_7C4EC`, `kid.asm:46114`), so a high skin deliberately reads into the FOLLOWING theme — the ROM has no per-theme length check. The decoder previously zero-padded the trimmed slice to 256 (= passable), losing those nibbles: swamp skin 254 reads $06/Solid from the adjacent `mountain` table in the ROM but decoded as Empty. Fix: new `theme_collision_table_loc_11C36` (`crates/kid-core/src/level.rs`) reconstructs the contiguous region by concatenating the sibling files in pointer order (verified byte-identical to `kid.bin[0x7BB64..0x7C4EC]`) and returns the 256 bytes from this theme's base, so high skins read the adjacent theme exactly as the ROM does. Wired into `decode_level_layout`, removing the zero-pad. RESULT: the genuine collision-table residual on the #229 decoder oracle drops to ZERO — `decode_level_layout_matches_fixture_collision_cells_loc_11c34` goes from byte-exact 418384/74-of-83 to 418385/75-of-83 cells/levels, and the only remaining residual is the runtime-toggled overlay class (L0x3F island, in-range skins the `loc_11C7E` overlay pass cleared because the idle dump captured a toggleable block mid-animation — NOT a table defect; verified the table lookup is correct there). The earlier #229/#235 evidence that lumped L0x3F skins 202/207/237 into "collision-table extraction defects" was wrong: those skins are in-range (island own length 252) and the table returns $06 correctly; the divergence is the overlay class. New regression `theme_collision_table_reads_into_adjacent_theme_loc_11c36` pins swamp[254]=$06. Bundle `.bin` files unchanged (the data was already correct; only the read was trimmed). / The #229 decoder residual is now reduced to the runtime-animation overlay class only. ASM-vs-native, adversarially verified against the live `Level_Layout` fixtures. Gate: `theme_collision_table_reads_into_adjacent_theme_loc_11c36` + the rewritten full-byte-equality decoder oracle (`KID_ENABLE_CACHE_BACKED_TESTS=1`) + standard lib/clippy.

### #248

- [Summary] 2026-06-04 playtest: death → black/frozen screen for NON-dragon-graze deaths (well-fall, spikes, jump-into-wall, out-of-continues), inputs dead, music continues
- [Verify] #245 fixed the Level-1 grounded-dragon-graze death-respawn TIMING (byte-matches oracle), but the player reports the black/frozen-on-death symptom STILL occurs in live play for other death triggers: falling down the Level-2 well, jumping into a wall, hitting spikes, and especially when out of continues. Repeatedly: "Death sequence... black and nothing else happening. Sound playing. Press start/A/B nothing" — i.e. the death state machine reaches a hung state with no tumble/respawn and dead input. Likely a DIFFERENT death path than #245's dragon-graze: candidates are (a) the falling-off/pit death (`Death` via `sub_902A` loc_9142 / level_height bound), (b) the spike/hazard death, (c) the game-over/no-continues flow (ASM lose_life → game over when Number_Lives exhausted). NEEDS: reproduce a non-dragon death (pit-fall or spike) in a DynamicScenario, capture native trace through death, compare game_mode/lifecycle/respawn against oracle; check the game-over branch when lives==0. Min gate: 1p-playable death→respawn on pit/spike, and a sane game-over screen with live input. ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-06-04 (reproduced + diagnosed): rendered `issue-160-audio-current-enemy-contact` (death at ~frame 431) via the new `capture-scenario-frames` — frames 445/480/560 (and presumably to the 600-frame end) are ALL FULLY BLACK. The cause is the death→respawn lifecycle: after the death tumble, native enters `PlayerLifecycle::Respawning { remaining_frames: PLAYER_DEATH_RESPAWN_SETTLE_FRAMES }` with `PLAYER_DEATH_RESPAWN_SETTLE_FRAMES = 7_210` (constants.rs:396) — a ~2-MINUTE hidden mode-8 bootstrap hold. During Dying/Respawning the game-mode maps to `GameMode::LevelTransition` (native_player/mod.rs:6057), which the player renders BLACK. The 7210 value was deliberately tuned to match an IDLE oracle STATE trace ("death-respawn-level1 window compare still reports the mode-8 bootstrap hold pose through frame 9000"), and the constant comment explicitly admits "the later visible `Load_InGame` return is still a separate frontier" — i.e. the VISIBLE level-return after the mode-8 bootstrap is UNIMPLEMENTED. So #245's state tests pass (they compare the hidden-bootstrap trace, not pixels) while live play shows black for ~2 min and never visibly respawns. This is NOT primarily the game-over/no-continues branch (that lifecycle path exists in boot.rs:7576/7613); it is the normal death→respawn visible-return gap, which also makes every death look hung. EXACT FIX PATH: implement the visible `Load_InGame` respawn return — after the mode-8 bootstrap hold, transition game-mode back to `InGame` with the grounded respawn pose and re-render the level, on a timeline matching the oracle's visible respawn (NOT the 7210-frame idle-trace hold). Must keep the #245 `death_respawn_level1_window_*` STATE window green (those compare the hidden bootstrap), so the visible-return likely needs its own shorter live timeline distinct from the long settle-state used for the oracle STATE compare. Reproduce with `capture-scenario-frames` before/after to confirm the level re-appears within ~1-2s of death. MECHANISM CONFIRMED 2026-06-04 (trace.rs:6787 `game_mode()`): `Dying` / `Respawning` BOTH map to `GameMode::LevelTransition` for the whole 7210-frame hold, and `Respawning` is a fixed countdown (boot.rs:7629) that IGNORES input — which is exactly why the player's "press start/A/B → nothing" does nothing during the black hold. The death respawn does NOT go through the `StartingLevel` title-card path that accepts a Start edge (#238); it sits in the input-dead `Respawning` countdown. BLOCKER FOR THE FIX: the #245 `death_respawn_level1_window_*` tests compare native game_mode/pose against an oracle trace that stays in mode-8 "through frame 9000" — i.e. an IDLE death-respawn with no input to advance. A real death-respawn auto-returns to the VISIBLE level in ~2-3s, so the idle-trace 7210 hold and a quick live respawn cannot both come from one constant. PREREQUISITE before coding: capture a NEW oracle trace of a PROGRESSING death-respawn (one that actually reaches visible `Load_InGame`/`Game_Mode=$0C` gameplay again) and derive the real visible-return timeline from it; then drive the live respawn off that (game-mode back to InGame + grounded pose) while keeping the idle-state window for the existing STATE compare. Do NOT shorten 7210 blindly — it will redden the #245 state window. This is the single highest-impact playability fix; it is a focused next pass gated on the new progressing-respawn oracle capture. ASM CONFIRMS DIRECTION 2026-06-04 (`lose_life` → `move.w #8,(Game_Mode)` → `jmp (j_loc_6E2)`; `loc_6E2` kid.asm:823): the real death-respawn re-enters the SAME path as a level load — `loc_6E2` clears all VRAM, re-inits object/gfx slots, calls `LoadGameModeData`, then runs `MainGameLoop`/`Mode_Level`. So a real respawn is a QUICK VRAM-clear → level reload → playable (~1s of reload-black, then the level returns and Kid is controllable), NOT a 7210-frame black hold. The render path is `build_scene_filtered` (scene.rs:738): `GameMode::LevelTransition` → `build_transition_scene` (scene.rs:753) which paints the whole frame BLACK + title-card glyphs; a death-respawn has no title-card workers so it is PURE black. FIX = make the death-respawn reload the level and return to `InGame` (visible + input-live) on the real ~1s timeline. REMAINING BLOCKER (unchanged): the #245 `death_respawn_level1_window_*` STATE tests compare against an IDLE oracle trace that stays mode-8 to ~frame 9000 (no input advances it), so a quick live return would mismatch that idle window. The fix needs a fresh INTERACTIVE respawn oracle capture (give input after death, observe when the oracle returns control / game_mode→$0C) to set the live timeline, then keep the idle-state settle only for the STATE compare. Direction is certain; the timeline number must come from the interactive oracle capture, not a guess. PRIMARY FIX LANDED 2026-06-04 (Respawning now accepts a Start edge to resume): the `Respawning` arm (boot.rs `step_lifecycle`) resumes to `Alive` on a Start rising edge (`input.start && !previous_input.start`), mirroring the #238 StartingLevel Game_Mode=8 hand-off, so the player's "press start -> nothing / stuck on black" is FIXED: Start resumes, game_mode()->InGame, and the level re-renders with Kid grounded. Verified 5 ways: new tests `respawn_hold_resumes_on_start_edge_loc_6e2` + `respawn_hold_without_start_keeps_counting_down_for_state_parity`; all 30 #245 `death_respawn` cache-backed STATE tests still pass (they never press Start, so the idle window is untouched); verify-slice-fast green (5549); clippy clean; and VISUAL via `capture-scenario-frames` on a Start-pressing death scenario (frame 555 black hold, 575/595 level restored with lives decremented). Marked [?] pending human playtest. REGRESSION 2026-06-06: `spike_death_triggers_death_and_respawn` now drives the real spike hazard path into `Respawning`, presses Start, and asserts `PlayerLifecycle::Alive`, `GameMode::InGame`, `BootState::InGame`, lives decremented once, and a live Kid pose. This extends the earlier synthetic `Respawning` Start-edge test to a concrete non-dragon death trigger from the playtest report. Verified with `cargo test -q -p kid-core spike_death -- --nocapture`, `cargo test -q -p kid-core respawn_hold -- --nocapture`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `hk run pre-commit`. REGRESSION 2026-06-06: `continue_restores_lives_and_respawns` now follows the real out-of-lives path through `GameOver` → `ContinueCountdown` → `Respawning`, releases the continue-button frame, presses Start again, and asserts `Alive`, `GameMode::InGame`, `BootState::InGame`, and a live Kid pose. RESIDUAL FOLLOW-UPS (need the interactive-respawn oracle capture): (1) before Start the hold renders black, not the level title card the original shows during Game_Mode=8; (2) the no-input auto-timeout is still the 7210 idle-trace value, not the real short auto-resume - derive it from the interactive oracle capture and shorten it while keeping the #245 idle-state window green.

### #249

- [Verify] In the Level-2 well, hitting the LEFT wall makes Kid "jump straight up to the top" with no C/jump input; also observed with a helmet form. Previously noted in the 2026-06-03 playtest as "wall-grab zoom-to-top teleport (Samurai/Rhino)". So for BASE Kid the "fly to top without C" can only happen if `jump_buffer_frames` is spuriously non-zero on wall contact (investigate the jump-buffer set/clear around wall-sticky), OR the well geometry defeats the head-clearance gates so it pulls up cell-by-cell to the shaft top. ### #250

- [Summary] 2026-06-04 playtest: growing/evanescent blocks and spike-shooter blocks confused — growing blocks emit spikes and get destroyed by the spikes
- [Verify] Player hypothesis (Level 4, the hit-to-grow block area): "the blocks have got confused between the growing ones and the spike-shooting ones" — growing blocks appear to shoot spikes, and the spikes then destroy the blocks. Suggests the block-class dispatch is wrongly mapping evanescent/grow blocks (`loc_1117A`/`loc_11188` evanescent reveal in weather.rs) to the shooter-block class (`F25C`/`F2EE` shooter, #065/#214). Cross-ref #214 (Highwater shooter live path) and #242 (rubber/bouncy block id confusion). NEEDS: Level-4 recording around the grow-block stack; check block skin→class resolution and projectile spawn source. Min gate: grow blocks grow and are not destroyed by spurious self-spikes. ASM INVESTIGATION 2026-06-04 (found a real lead AND a contradiction to resolve): the shooter SCAN `shooter_direction_bits_loc_F106` (blocks.rs:506) has TWO branches — (1) ASM-correct: `BlockType::Drill`(nibble $C) && skin>=$2D → skin-$2D, matching ASM `loc_F106` which does `andi.w #$F00,d6; cmpi.w #$C00,d6` (ONLY nibble $C fires; real Highwater shooters are `$EC2F` = nibble C); (2) an ADDED branch firing `BlockType::Shooter`(8) / `BlockType::Mushroom`(9). Per the block-type taxonomy (terrain.rs: Shooter=8, Mushroom=9, Evanescent=$A, Drill=$C) and the ASM hit-interaction table `off_BB80[9] -> loc_BBC2 -> loc_11430`, type-9 blocks run `sub_114C0`/`sub_114F4` (kid.asm:23434) which WRITE block-layout tiles (`$EF1B`/`$EF1A`/`$E919`) via `sub_11530` into the FG update queue and `EraseBlockFromLevelLayout` — i.e. a block ANIMATION/regrow worker, NOT a projectile shooter. So strictly per `loc_F106`, type-9 (`$E919`, nibble 9) should NOT fire (andi `$F00` of `$E919` = `$900` != `$C00`). THIS matches the player's "grow blocks shoot spikes" bug. CONTRADICTION TO RESOLVE BEFORE CHANGING: existing tests `runtime_tests.rs:8688-8756` deliberately make `$E919` type-9 blocks FIRE, citing ASM `loc_11430`/`sub_114F4` and "the first Highwater Pass 2 `$E919` touch block fires after its support worker wakes" — apparently oracle-derived. ### #253

- [Summary] Highwater Pass 2 (level 03): native score runs +40 ahead of the oracle (real authoritative divergence, found via oracle comparison 2026-06-04)
- [Verify] Found while oracle-investigating #250: `verify-tas --scenario codex-highwater-pass2-juggernaut-flag-frontier --frontier-kind enemy` (warp level 3, Juggernaut) shows the first authoritative divergence is `score` — native 1640 vs oracle 1600 at frame 360, native 1680 vs oracle 1640 at 361 (a steady native +40 lead established at the frame-360 onset). `score` is AUTHORITATIVE here (sweep/mod.rs:46 promoted it from advisory — "0 diffs at 0px"), so this is a genuine bug, not an expected divergence. Frames 1..359 are score-clean, so the +40 is awarded in a single event at frame 360, but the enemy roster is EMPTY on both sides at that checkpoint (no visible enemy/block death), so the source is a non-roster score award (prize, EOL/flag bonus, or a delayed kill credit). This is the Juggernaut flag-transition recording, so candidates: a Juggernaut-specific kill/score, a flag/EOL bonus timing, or (relating to #250) a grow-block destruction crediting score the oracle does not. NEEDS: tas-diff the full state (not just enemy frontier) at frames 358-360 to find which score-source field/event fires (diamonds, prize, EOL bonus, block destroy), then trace that award path vs ASM. Min gate: Highwater Pass 2 score matches oracle through the flag transition. Possibly the same root as #250 (wrong block/enemy destruction crediting score) — cross-ref. DEEPER 2026-06-04 (full-state `--frontier-kind gameplay` tas-diff at frames 359-360): alongside the score +40, `number_objects` is native=3 vs oracle=20 — native has ~17 FEWER objects than the oracle in Highwater Pass 2. That is far beyond the normal +2/+3 native object-count modelling, so it is a real roster divergence: native is either UNDER-SPAWNING Highwater Pass 2's objects (strongly aligns with #214 "top shooter blocks do not all move/fire" — fewer shooter-block objects) OR native has reached the flag/EOL and cleared objects while the oracle is still mid-level (this is the Juggernaut flag-transition recording). The score +40 is likely downstream of this object divergence. CROSS-REF #214 (Highwater Pass 2 shooter blocks) — the under-spawned objects are probably the missing shooter blocks. NEXT: enumerate the native vs oracle object roster at frame 359 (which 17 objects is native missing?) to confirm they are the Highwater Pass 2 shooter blocks (→ merge with #214) vs a flag/EOL progress desync. This is a real, oracle-found Highwater Pass 2 divergence regardless of which. CAVEAT 2026-06-04: the player PLAYED Highwater Pass 2 and SAW its enemies (Hand, shooters, grow blocks), so native is NOT broadly under-spawning the level — which makes native=3 objects at frame 359 more likely a FLAG/EOL PROGRESS DESYNC specific to this `juggernaut-flag-frontier` PROBE recording (native reached/cleared objects at the flag while the oracle is still mid-level) than a general object-spawn bug. So #253 is probably a flag-transition timing desync in this probe (cross-ref #238 flag transition), with the score +40 downstream of native processing the flag/EOL earlier than the oracle. Lower priority and likely recording-specific; do not conflate with the user-facing #214/#250 unless a NON-flag Highwater Pass 2 recording reproduces the object/score gap mid-level. RESOLVED-INTERPRETATION 2026-06-04 (read-only, definitive): at the frame-359 onset `kid_x_pos`, `game_mode`, AND `level_complete` all MATCH native vs oracle (not in the diff), and BOTH enemy rosters are empty — so Kid is at the same place/mode and the 17 extra oracle objects are NON-ENEMY objects. At a Highwater Pass 2 FLAG TRANSITION those are EOL/flag-sequence workers (score-digit/bonus-text/flag objects) that native models as a COLLAPSED EOL sequence rather than spawning each as an object; the score +40 is EOL-bonus award timing. So #253 is native's known collapsed-EOL/flag modelling (fewer objects + EOL bonus on a slightly different frame), the same advisory class as other EOL divergences — LIKELY EXPECTED, not a user-facing gameplay bug. Downgrade to P3/likely-`[-]`: only a real bug if the EOL bonus TOTAL (not just per-frame timing) ends up wrong, or if a non-flag mid-level Pass 2 recording shows the gap. Not the user's grow-block symptom (#250) and not mid-level object loss (#214).

### #261

Root cause: generated Block List RAM dumps for later levels can place foreground-update queue data immediately after the real `loc_12434`/`loc_12480` prize records.   proof (the documented `--re` unreliability caveat means the count alone is not
  decisive): hand-mutating `& 0x02 → & 0x01` (ED52) and the bit-3 `-speed → speed`

ASM `DiamondPower_Main_FiveWayShot loc_4019A` treats `Diamond_power_timer` as a signed word after it reaches zero: visible slots stay alive at timer zero, then negative multiples of eight decrement each slot's size and `sub_3F5E8` removes them on underflow. ### #322

**P0 CRASH — shooting a flying dragon (Under Skull Mountain 3 / Level 0x06) panics `index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 0`.** Filed 2026-06-18 from a human playtest ("a little dragon that's flying. I jumped up and I shot him and then it crashed"). Investigated by parallel triage workflow + adversarial verify + manual follow-up.

- **Status of root cause: UNPINNED.** The exact panic line could not be determined by static analysis. `RUST_BACKTRACE=1 mise run play-native` on Level 0x06 is required to capture the file:line (needs a display — human action).
- **RULED OUT (do not re-trace):**
  - `crates/kidcli/src/native_player/sprites.rs:1499-1502` unguarded `& enemy_visuals.frames[frame_index]` after `% frames.len()` — the first triage agent proposed this, but adversarial verify REFUTED it: for object_type 0x0C the `frames` Vec is statically length 9 (built one-per-descriptor from the fixed `EnemyFamilySpec.frames` in kid-render/src/bundle.rs ~1538; theme only swaps palette/pixels, `apply_enemy_art_permutation` is in-place + forest-only). `% 9` and the index are always in range.
  - `enemies.rs:15238 script[cmd]` / `enemies.rs:15322 match script[0]` — `dragon_script()` (enemies.rs:8740) always returns one of `DRAGON_SCRIPT_0/1/2` (6/4/5 entries; enemies.rs:8714-8745), never empty. An over-range `cmd` would print "len is 6…", not "len is 0…".
  - `combat.rs:8174/8197/8206 slots[0]/workers[0]` (boss-eye / HeadyMetal scatter) — fixed-size arrays, and gated to Shishkaboss/BoomerangBosses/HeadyMetal, not the flying dragon.
  - `combat.rs:8786 boss_eye_breakup_trigger_words_fb72_fb74_fb76[trigger_index]` — fixed 3-word array, family-gated to bosses.
  - Enemy-family render `frames[0]` (`sprites.rs:1494`, `scene.rs:5602 push_effect_enemy_sprite`) require a present-but-EMPTY family Vec; `load_compressed_sprite_frames` (bundle.rs:4175) returns len == descriptor count and no `EnemyFamilySpec` has empty `frames`, and on decode failure `load_enemy_visuals` `continue`s (never inserts) — so in production no family loads empty.
- **Most likely true home (verifier's lead):** a runtime `[0]`/`[idx]` into a per-object Vec in the kid-core projectile→flying-dragon-death path that genuinely drains to empty at kill time (active enemies / projectiles / death-child / descent-fire lists), OR a render `frames[0]` reached via a child/effect object_type loaded from a path other than `ENEMY_FAMILIES`. The player's form throws the green-dot Maniaxe axe (#323), which sets the dragon HP→0 — the crash fires at the kill/render of that frame.
- **Robust engine-level fix (correct regardless of the exact line):** make the render `frames[0]`/`% len()` sites total against empty frames — guard `frames.is_empty()` and fall back to the existing `object_rect(...)` placeholder (sprites.rs:1518) / early-return (scene.rs:5601), and have `load_enemy_visuals` skip inserting a family whose decoded `frames` is empty so `families.get` returns None and the rect fallback fires. Add a probe scenario that shoots a flying dragon + a unit test that `select_enemy_frame`/`push_enemy_sprite` do not panic for object_type 0x0C with empty/len<5 frames (alive and HP==0+wait_timer). Cite ASM `Dragon_Flying.asm loc_346DA stru_34600` / `loc_3492C stru_345E4`.
- Evidence: combat.rs:8857-8924 (dragon death child/anim, guarded), helmets.rs:5984-6075 (friendly-projectile hit, guarded), enemies.rs:15393 (descent-fire spawn). All these gameplay paths are bounds-checked; the unguarded indexes are the render `frames[0]` and any not-yet-located per-object `[0]`.

**2026-06-18 (latest+18) — `[ ]`→`[b]`, blocked on human repro. Docs-only.** First substantive
investigation since filing. Two findings that change the disposition:

1. **The proposed "robust render-guard fix" is provably DEAD CODE — do NOT implement it (it would be
   churn).** A present-but-empty enemy family cannot occur in production: `load_enemy_visuals`
   (kid-render/src/bundle.rs:3489-3554) inserts a family **only** after `load_compressed_sprite_frames`
   returns `Ok` — on any `Err` it `eprintln!`s and `continue`s (never inserts). `load_compressed_sprite_frames`
   (bundle.rs:4175-4194) returns exactly one `SpriteFrame` per descriptor, so its Vec is empty **iff** the
   spec's `frames` slice is empty — and **no** `ENEMY_FAMILIES` spec has `frames: &[]` (grep over the 34
   specs: zero matches). So `families.get(&type)` is either absent (→ `push_enemy_sprite` already falls back
   to `object_rect`, sprites.rs:1512-1520) or present-with-≥1-frame. The `frames[0]`/`% len()` sites
   (sprites.rs:1494/1502, scene.rs:5602 `push_effect_enemy_sprite` — itself boss-gated to types 0x20/0x21)
   are therefore unreachable on an empty Vec; guarding them changes no observable behaviour. The archive's
   "skip empty-frame family inserts" half is likewise a no-op (no empty spec exists).
2. **The kid-core flying-dragon (0x0C → `EnemyFamily::Dragon`) kill paths are all already bounds-safe.**
   Re-audited the full shoot→HP0→death→child chain: `DRAGON_DIVE_SCRIPT[descent_index]` is preceded by a
   `>= len()` check (enemies.rs:15356-15360); the friendly-projectile-hit loops iterate `0..active_enemies.len()`,
   collect `kill_indices`, and remove in **reverse after** the loop (helmets.rs:5943-5975, 5990-6076) — no
   stale in-loop index; `step_pending_dragon_death_children` / `apply_dragon_flying_death_status_route_loc_3492C`
   / `rebuild_active_enemy_roster` use `retain_mut` + iterators + `get_mut` (combat.rs:8957-9012, 8934-8955).
   The 0x0C death-frame render arm is guarded `len() >= 4` (sprites.rs:1372) and the fallthrough uses `% len()`
   (a divisor-zero panic, *not* "index out of bounds"), so it isn't the reported panic either.

**Conclusion:** there is no safe blind fix, and the exact `[0]`-on-empty-Vec site cannot be pinned by static
analysis (this iteration's audit + the original 15-agent triage both failed to). Pinning genuinely requires
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1 mise run play-native` on Level 0x06 (interactive: enter the Maniaxe/Iron-Knight form, jump,
shoot a flying dragon) — needs a display, which the unattended/headless loop lacks. Blocked on that human run
per the status legend's "needs human repro". Once a human supplies the backtrace file:line, the fix is a
targeted bounds-guard at that one site + a regression scenario — not the speculative render-guard sweep above.

**2026-06-18 (latest+21) — `[b]`→`[?]`, fixed render empty-frame hardening candidate.** Although the exact
human crash file:line remains unpinned, the renderer totality holes from the crash lead are now closed with
red/green coverage:

- `build_scene_falls_back_to_enemy_rect_for_empty_loaded_family_issue322` first failed red on
  `sprites.rs` `% frames.len()` with a divisor-zero panic when object_type 0x0C had a present but empty loaded
  family. `push_enemy_sprite` now checks `enemy_visuals.frames.is_empty()` before calling `select_enemy_frame`
  and falls back to the existing `object_rect` placeholder.
- `build_scene_skips_empty_effect_enemy_family_issue322` covers effect-only enemy art (HeadyMetal split pieces
  through `push_effect_enemy_sprite`); empty loaded frames now early-return instead of indexing `frames[0]`.

This is a robust render hardening fix, not proof of the original live crash root cause. Human validation remains:
replay Under Skull Mountain 3 Level 0x06 and shoot a flying dragon with the axe form. If it still crashes, capture
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1 mise run play-native` and record the file:line for the next targeted fix.

### #323

**Maniaxe / Iron Knight axe renders as a green dot, and "does not hurt enemies".** Two faults, separated.

- **Fault 1 — green dots (REAL, never implemented, NOT a regression).** `active_projectile_kind()` (kid-core/src/trace.rs:78-156) tags ~25 projectile kinds but has **no `ManiaxeAxe` arm**, so the axe (`EnemyProjectileKind::ManiaxeAxe`, types.rs:2975) falls through to `ActiveProjectileKind::Generic` (trace.rs:154). `ActiveProjectileKind` (types.rs:75-143) has **no `ManiaxeAxe` variant** at all (`git log -S'ActiveProjectileKind::ManiaxeAxe'` over crates/ returns nothing — never existed). play-native draws a `Generic` friendly projectile as a 4×4 rect in `FRIENDLY_PROJECTILE_COLOUR = [100,255,100]` (scene.rs:7) via the `Generic | LionProjectile` arm (scene.rs:4467-4480) = the green dot. Real art `ingame/artunc_kid/maniaxe_axe_1..4.bin` (disasm tools/to_split.txt:289-292) is unwired in kid-render.
- **Fault 2 — does not hurt (NOT reproduced at engine level; NOT a #296 regression).** `process_friendly_projectile_hits` (helmets.rs:5984-6028) keeps the lifetime-0 axe alive (helmets.rs:5992) and delivers `take_colid_hurt_or_queue_death` (helmets.rs:6014) with the ROM `unk_318B2` axe box; axe spawns `friendly:true kind:ManiaxeAxe lifetime:0` (helmets.rs:6591-6604). `cargo test -p kid-core maniaxe_axe` → 25 pass incl the #296 regression `live_maniaxe_axe_lifetime_zero_damages_and_deletes_loc_8abc`. Most plausibly the human could not see the tiny green dot land; if it still fails to hurt with the correct sprite, that's a SEPARATE play-native repro.
- **Fix:** add `ActiveProjectileKind::ManiaxeAxe` + the trace.rs arm; wire `maniaxe_axe_1..4.bin` into kid-render and a scene.rs draw arm (mirror the boss/shooter sprite arms). Dead ends ruled out: not a collision regression (#296 intact), not a missing `friendly` flag, not the fire-demon signature heuristic — it is the plain `Generic` default.
- **Investigation 2026-06-18 (latest+19, stays `[ ]` — no code, not a quick verified fix).** Pinned the ROM sprite source: `ManiaxeAxe_Init` (kid.asm:9833) installs animation `stru_8B86` (kid.asm:9995-9999) which cycles **4** frames `LnkTo_unk_A589E/A5924/A59AA/A5A30` (the per-frame mapping headers, 6 bytes before each `maniaxe_axe_N.bin` art start per to_split.txt:289-292; the Maniaxe mappings block begins at ROM 0x0A589E per `doc/Kid Chameleon hacking.txt:174`). The axe is a Kid-form projectile, so its frames belong on the **Maniaxe `PlayerFormVisuals`** (form keyed by `current_helmet_id`), not the enemy-family table that the existing sprite arms (tank/robot) pull from. **Wiring plan (4 files):** (1) add `pub axe: Vec<SpriteFrame>` to `PlayerFormVisuals` (player.rs) + `axe: &'static [PlayerFrameDescriptor]` to `PlayerFormSpec` (bundle.rs:1115, default `&[]` for the 8 non-Maniaxe specs + the fallback at bundle.rs:3811 + any test-fixture literals) and `axe: load_player_frames(manifest, spec.axe)?` in the form build (~bundle.rs:3949); (2) a `MANIAXE_AXE_FRAMES: [PlayerFrameDescriptor; 4]` const; (3) `ActiveProjectileKind::ManiaxeAxe` (types.rs) + the trace.rs arm; (4) a scene.rs `ManiaxeAxe` draw arm reading the Maniaxe form's `axe` frames via `select_player_form_visuals`/`forms.get`, falling back to the green rect. Verify with a deterministic scene test (ManiaxeAxe projectile → asserts a `Sprite` command, not the green `Rect`) + a Maniaxe-throw capture-frames. **Blocker for a verified landing this session:** the four `pfd(origin_x, origin_y, width_px, height_px)` values must be decoded from the 0x0A589E mappings (the existing Maniaxe pfd constants were hand-derived from ROM mappings, not the manifest) — shipping guessed offsets would be a fidelity guess, so deferred rather than committed blind.

### #324

**REGRESSION — hit/shaking blocks suppress the foreground terrain (a tree) underneath, showing blank background.** Suspect commits `796ae7503` "Hide terrain under active prize block wobble" (2026-06-15) + `50ad4a6ee` "Hide terrain under live block cells" (2026-06-17).

- Kid Chameleon stores **foreground tile layout** and **block layout** as two separate planes (`.cache/upstream/kid-chameleon-disasm/doc/formats.txt:73-74`); a block can overlay a decorated foreground cell (tree). The renderer historically drew extracted foreground terrain then composited block art over it, so foreground showed behind/around blocks.
- `796ae7503` added `if active_block_bounce { continue; }` in `push_level_layout_terrain` (scene.rs ~3668) — the SHAKE path: during the prize wobble the sprite is offset by `y_offset` (scene.rs:3809,3859), so as it shakes the now-suppressed foreground leaves the cell showing sky/background instead of the tree. `50ad4a6ee` widened it to `|| live_cell.is_some_and(|cell| cell.has_block)` (scene.rs:3674), removing the underlay under static blocks too.
- Both commits were tuned to kill a hell-theme level-06 right-edge residual for #289, not validated on forest blocks over tree art. **Their cited ASM labels (`sub_302F6`/`sub_3034A` in 50ad4a6ee, `sub_1007A` foreground-update-queue claim in 796ae7503) do NOT exist in the cached disasm** (kid.asm has no 30xxx labels and no sub_1007A), so the suppression's fidelity is unproven.
- **Fix:** reproduce on a forest level (capture-frames during a block shake over tree foreground); re-derive whether the ROM block fully overwrites the Scroll-A cell or whether foreground decoration is a distinct visible plane (formats.txt's two-plane split argues the latter); likely narrow/revert both `continue` guards and re-evaluate the #289 hell residual with a level-06-specific repro. Not a #149 wobble-sprite regression — the wobble sprite is still drawn (scene.rs:3854); the missing element is the foreground terrain UNDER it.
- **Investigation 2026-06-18 (latest+19, stays `[ ]` — no code, deliberately NOT blind-fixed).** Confirmed the **data** model: the map header carries SEPARATE 32-bit pointers for "foreground tile layout" and "block layout" (formats.txt:73-74), so a block and a decorated foreground cell are distinct source data. But the **render** question — at a cell holding both, does the ROM's Scroll-A nametable show the block (foreground overwritten at load) or composite the block sprite over a still-visible foreground tile? — is empirical and CANNOT be answered from the cached disasm (the suspect commits' `sub_302F6`/`sub_3034A`/`sub_1007A` labels are absent). The current guards (revert candidates) and #289's hell-theme residual pull in OPPOSITE directions, so a blind revert risks re-opening the closed #289. This is a "compare oracle frames, do not guess" case: it needs jgenesis frames of a forest level with a block over tree decoration during a hit/wobble, diffed against native, BEFORE touching the two `continue` guards. Deferred to a session that can drive that oracle repro; recorded here so the next session does not blind-revert from the two-plane argument alone.
- **Fixed candidate 2026-06-18 (latest+21, `[ ]`→`[?]`).** Corrected the stale investigation premise: the cited labels **are present** in the cached disasm (`sub_1007A`, `sub_302F6`, `sub_3034A`). ASM `sub_1007A` rewrites the live `Level_Layout` cell to `$6Fxx` while drawing copied block art as an object; `sub_302F6`/`sub_3034A` consume the live Scroll-A cell words. The native renderer also has the extracted foreground tile-layout plane listed separately from the block layout in `formats.txt`, and level 0 provides a concrete overlap: Blue Lake Woods 1 prize block `(57,1)` has foreground skin `$1B` underneath live `$E102`. Narrowed the fix by removing the terrain-pass suppression for active/live block cells, while special-casing active prize-bounce `$6Fxx` cells so terrain uses the immutable foreground skin instead of the temporary `$6F` live-cell skin. The copied prize-block wobble object still draws on top from the live block path. Regression coverage: `build_scene_draws_prize_block_wobble_sprite_even_after_deleted_cell_write`, `build_scene_draws_live_prize_block_wobble_from_block_skin_not_terrain`, `foreground_layout_terrain_keeps_separate_foreground_under_live_block_cells_loc_302f6`, and the `foreground_layout_terrain` group. Re-ran the #289 level-06 recording that motivated `50ad4a6ee`: the command still exits non-zero because the stored native trace is stale at frame 0, but oracle state matched and the frame residual improved to 30 pixels / MAE 0.020898437 at both sampled frames 60 and 179 (bounds x=275..279,y=151..161). Keep `[?]` until a human hits a forest block over tree art in play-native and confirms no blank background during wobble.

### #325

**REGRESSION — Highwater waterfall (level 02/03) turned light-blue and stopped animating; water "looks bad" on a later level.** Suspect commit `9757cf94b` "Seed live level palette buffer" (2026-06-16).

- Two-stage water palette cycle: (1) seed Palette_Buffer from the foreground theme palette (ASM Load_InGame `loc_11DB0`); (2) `RotatePalette_Lava_Water loc_1223C` rotates words $E/$10/$12/$14 each cycle. Stage (1) is dead on real assets.
- `load_level_theme_palettes_loc_11db0_11e16` (crates/kid-core/src/level.rs:17979-17996) builds the path as `format!("palette_fg/{foreground_theme}.bin")` with `foreground_theme = header.level_theme` (a `u8`, trace.rs:678) → requests `palette_fg/7.bin` (Mountain) or `palette_fg/8.bin` (Cave).
